Ross Vintcent scored two tries, with Sam Harris, Henry Slade and Bachuki Tchumbadze adding one each, and Slade kicked three conversions and a penalty.

Max Hicks scored Newcastle's other try, with Zack Henry converting all four to earn two bonus points. Newcastle led 21-19 at half-time, and full-back Jake Dalziel became the club's youngest ever league debutant at 18 years and 54 days. Exeter lost Immanuel Feyi-Waboso to a leg problem, and Newcastle prop Adam Brocklebank was sin-binned late on.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. A hat-trick from Newcastle wing Christian Wade was not enough to stop Exeter claiming their first Gallagher Prem win of the season as they edged a topsy-turvy game at Sandy Park 34-28.

The lead frequently changed hands and it was not until the dying stages that the Chiefs were able to seal victory. Max Hicks scored Newcastle’s other try, with Zack Henry converting all four to secure two valuable bonus points.

Rugby.title: Sale complete late win to leave Harlequins bottom of table
Rugby.summary: Sale 28-24 Harlequins: Marcus Smith’s tries threaten a schok result but Sale came back to win
bullets: Sale beat Harlequins 28-24 at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford, sealing victory with a 73rd-minute penalty try, to leave Quins bottom of the Prem after a third successive defeat. Marcus Smith, returning from a finger injury, scored two tries in the opening quarter, and Quins led 17-14 at half-time having had two tries disallowed.

Sale, who had lost on the opening day to Bristol, have now beaten Saracens and Harlequins in successive weeks, and it was their fifth straight win against Quins in the league and Europe. Jason Gilmore's side made seven changes after a 48-0 defeat by Gloucester, their worst league loss in 26 years. Hooker Sam Riley, who scored two tries, was sin-binned for the infringement that led to the penalty try.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Harlequins’ troubled start to the Gallagher Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford.

The Sharks left it late but came from behind to snatch a 28-24 success with a 73rd-minute penalty try, after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to threaten a shock win for the visitors.

Rugby.title: Late Sale penalty try continues Harlequins woes
Rugby.summary: Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continues with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium.
bullets: Harlequins lost a third successive Prem game, going down to Sale at CorpAcq Stadium after a 73rd-minute penalty try. Marcus Smith, back from a finger injury, scored two tries in the opening quarter, and Quins led 17-14 at half-time, with two further tries ruled out by the television match official. The result leaves Quins bottom of the table.

Sale, who also beat Saracens last week, scored through Elia Canakaivata, Gus Warr and Ben Bamber, and won with a rumbling maul that drove Quins back 30 metres. Referee Christophe Ridley awarded the penalty try and sent hooker Sam Riley to the sin-bin. Harlequins, beaten 48-0 by Gloucester the previous weekend, now face Vannes at home in the Challenge Cup next week.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium. The Sharks came from behind to win the game with a 73rd-minute penalty try after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to give Quins an early lead.

After their opening-day reverse to Bristol at home, Sale have bounced back strongly with back-to-back wins over Saracens and Quins. Despite their first points of the season, the loss leaves Quins rooted to the foot of the table.

Rugby.title: Wade scores 100th Prem try as Newcastle lose to Exeter
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade becomes just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 loss at Exeter.
bullets: Christian Wade became the second player to score 100 Premiership Rugby tries, claiming a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter. The 35-year-old scored twice in the first half, the second giving Newcastle a two-point half-time lead, and added a third early in the second half after a Henry Slade error. He is now one short of the all-time record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023.

Exeter secured a bonus-point first win of the season through tries from Ross Vintcent, who scored after 38 seconds on his return from injury, Sam Harris and Bachuki Tchumbadze, plus a 64th-minute Slade penalty. The result keeps Exeter eighth, four points behind leaders Gloucester, while winless Newcastle are second-from-bottom. A crowd of 7,071 meant Sandy Park's North Terrace was closed for the first time for a Prem game.
Rugby.copy:
Christian Wade became just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter. Wade, 35, went over twice in the first half - his second giving the Red Bulls a two-point half-time lead - before pouncing on a Henry Slade error to race in for a third early in the second half.

Newcastle's former England winger is now just one try off the all-time Prem try record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023. Wade, who spent four years trying to break into the NFL from 2018, returned to the Prem in 2024 with Gloucester after two years at French side Racing 92, last year moving to Newcastle after a brief spell at rugby league's Wigan Warriors.

Rugby.title: Davies urged to reverse retirement for World Cup
Rugby.summary: Ex-Wales hooker Scott Baldwin is convinced the 36-year-old's World Cup know-how can still help Wales in Australia.
bullets: Former Wales hooker Scott Baldwin has urged scrum-half Gareth Davies to reverse his international retirement for the 2027 World Cup. Davies, 36, retired from Test rugby in 2024 but came off the bench to spark a Scarlets comeback from 21-7 down against Benetton in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday, securing the club's first win of the season.

Baldwin told BBC Radio Wales Sport that Davies could be valuable in a World Cup quarter-final against England, questioning Wales' depth behind Tomos Williams. Davies won 77 caps and toured twice with the British and Irish Lions, and will be 37 at the tournament, where Wales face Zimbabwe, Tonga and England in Pool F. Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies praised his contribution as "superb".
Rugby.copy:
Gareth Davies has been urged to rethink his international retirement for the 2027 World Cup by former Wales team-mate Scott Baldwin. The 36-year-old scrum-half sparked a Scarlets comeback from 21-7 down to beat Benetton in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday.

Davies retired from Test rugby in 2024 but ex-Wales hooker Baldwin believes the veteran could still thrive at a fourth World Cup next year. "He could be just what you want in a quarter-final of a World Cup, in a Wales-England fixture in 12 months' time," Baldwin told BBC Radio Wales Sport.

Rugby.title: Fight for Wales spots heats up as under-threat regions win
Rugby.summary: The talking points from round three of URC as Ospreys and Scarlets get first win and players try to impress Wales boss Steve Tandy.
Rugby.copy:
There was western relief after Ospreys and Scarlets got up and running in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) season. The two sides are playing amid uncertainty over their futures under controversial Welsh Rugby Union plans, yet produced the goods on the pitch in round three.

Ospreys won an engrossing derby against Dragons at Rodney Parade, inflicting a first defeat of the season on their hosts, while Scarlets sneaked past Benetton thanks to Sam Costelow's late penalty.

Rugby.title: Ulster playing games like training sessions
Rugby.summary: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
Rugby.copy:
Head coach Richie Murphy says Ulster are "playing matches like they're training sessions" as he expressed his disappointment with his side's slow start in Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.

Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.

Rugby.title: Leinster stroll past Cardiff for happy homecoming
Rugby.summary: Champions Leinster score five tries to beat Cardiff in Dublin for their first win of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship campaign.
Rugby.copy:
Champions Leinster made a successful return to the revamped Laya Arena by beating Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship (URC). The Irish province recorded their first victory of the 2026-27 season in front of 20,600 supporters, and condemned the Blue and Blacks to a first loss.

Leinster scored three tries inside the first quarter through Hugo Keenan, Jimmy O'Brien and Jack Conan, then O'Brien's second in the 37th minute secured the four-try bonus. But, with a raft of Ireland internationals making their first outings of the campaign, the second half was flat and scoreless until Jamie Osborne went over with five minutes to go.

Rugby.title: Caluori scores as Saracens too strong for Bristol
Rugby.summary: Noah Caluori gets on the scoresheet as Saracens continue their hold over Bristol Bears at the StoneX Stadium with a 30-7 victory.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: Caluori, O'Driscoll, penalty, J. Bracken Cons: Farrell Pens: Farrell 2 Saracens continued their hold over Bristol Bears at the StoneX Stadium with a convincing 30-7 victory.

Bristol have now failed to win in all eight of their Prem visits to Saracens' home since they reached the top flight, with this loss also their first defeat of the 2026-27 campaign.

Rugby.title: Edinburgh top URC after bonus-point win over Zebre
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh go top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre makes it three wins from three.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: M. Currie, Douglas, Bradbury, T. Currie Cons: Grayson 3 Pens: Grayson Edinburgh went top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre made it three wins from three for Sean Everitt's injury-hit side.

James Grayson kicked a penalty to put the visitors in front early on, but after winger Malelili Satala was sin-binned for a deliberate knock-on, Italy scrum-half Alessandro Fusco put Zebre in front with the game's first try.

Racket.title: Sonay Kartal +120 in WTA Rankings as she makes history by reaching Wuhan Open final
Racket.summary: Kartal stunned Jelena Ostapenko to continue her remarkable run in Wuhan. The post Sonay Kartal +120 in WTA Rankings as she makes history by reaching Wuhan Open final appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Sonay Kartal beat world No 34 Jelena Ostapenko 7-6(9), 7-6(5) in the Wuhan Open semi-finals on Saturday to reach the biggest final of her career at the WTA 1000 event. She recovered from a double break down at 1-4 in the first set and from 1-4 in the second, saving three set points in each set before winning both tie-breaks. She is the lowest-ranked player to reach a WTA 1000 final since the category was introduced in 1990.

The 24-year-old is ranked 170th and is competing on a protected ranking after missing more than six months through injury this year. Her run has earned 650 ranking points, taking her total to 1,097 and lifting her 120 places to world No 50 in the Live WTA Rankings. Her career-high ranking is 44th, reached in July 2025.
Racket.copy:
Sonay Kartal made history as she upset Jelena Ostapenko in an enthralling contest to reach the biggest final of her career at the 2026 Wuhan Open. The Brit prevailed 7-6(9), 7-6(5) over world No 34 Ostapenko in the semi-finals at the WTA 1000 tournament in China on Saturday.

In the first set, Kartal recovered from being a double break down at 1-4 and saved three set points before winning a pulsating tiebreak. Kartal was broken in the second game of the second set, but remarkably, she fought back from a 1-4 deficit again and survived three set points on her serve before sealing victory in the tiebreak.

Racket.title: Sonay Kartal: British star digs deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final
Racket.summary: Sonay Kartal: British star digs deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final Sky Sports
bullets: Britain's Sonay Kartal beat Jelena Ostapenko 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) in the Wuhan Open semi-finals on Saturday to reach her first WTA 1000 final, becoming only the second British woman after Johanna Konta to do so. Ranked 170th, she is the lowest-ranked player to reach the final in Wuhan, despite Ostapenko hitting 50 winners. She will face either Iga Swiatek or Maja Chwalinska in the final on Sunday.

Kartal, 24, is playing only her third tournament since returning from a stress fracture in her back that kept her out for six months, including Wimbledon. Her run has included wins over Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini and Elina Svitolina, and she will move inside the top 50 to become British No 1. She described the semi-final as one of the toughest matches she has played and one of her best mental performances.
Racket.copy:
Sonay Kartal defeats Jelena Ostapenko to reach her first-ever WTA 1000 final against former world No 1 Iga Swiatek or French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska; You can watch the WTA Wuhan Open final - live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 11.30am

Britain's Sonay Kartal was forced to dig deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final on Saturday. Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Ostapenko.

Racket.title: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina speaks out after stunning Alexander Zverev at Shanghai Masters
Racket.summary: Davidovich Fokina has spoken about his mindset change after upsetting Zverev. The post Alejandro Davidovich Fokina speaks out after stunning Alexander Zverev at Shanghai Masters appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina beat world No 2 Alexander Zverev 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 in the Shanghai Masters semi-finals on Saturday. After being broken in the 11th game of the first set, the Spaniard lost only nine points on serve across the 10 service games he played in the second and third sets. He now trails Zverev 2-6 in their meetings.

The world No 26 has won nine of his last 10 matches, a run that began with his title at the ATP 250 event in Chengdu, and climbs 11 places to No 15 in the Live ATP Rankings. He will play either Daniil Medvedev or Rafael Jodar in the final, seeking a third ATP Tour title and a first Masters 1000 crown. He said his time out injured this summer had given him time to rethink, as he had previously not been enjoying tennis and had been very frustrated.
Racket.copy:
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina has spoken about how his mindset has changed after his stunning win against world No 2 Alexander Zverev at the 2026 Shanghai Masters. World No 26 Davidovich Fokina downed Zverev 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 in the semi-finals at the ATP Masters 1000 tournament in Shanghai on Saturday. He now holds a 2-6 record against Zverev

After he was broken in the 11th game of the first set, Davidovich Fokina lost only nine points in the 10 service games he played across the second and third sets. The Spaniard has now won nine of his last 10 matches in a run that started with his title run at the ATP 250 event in Chengdu.

Racket.title: Kartal reaches Wuhan final as dream week continues
Racket.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal beats former French Open winner Jelena Ostapenko to reach the Wuhan Open final in only her third event after a six-month injury lay-off.
bullets: Sonay Kartal beat former Grand Slam champion Jelena Ostapenko 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) in the Wuhan Open semi-final to reach the biggest final of her career, a WTA 1,000 event. The 24-year-old British number five is playing only her third event since returning from a six-month back injury absence. She trailed 4-1 in both sets and saved three set points in each.

Kartal, ranked 170th, is the lowest-ranked player to reach a WTA 1,000 final since the format was introduced in 1990. She was ranked 54th before her lay-off. She said it was one of the toughest matches she had played and described it as one of the best mental performances of her career. She will play either Iga Swiatek or Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's final.
Racket.copy:
Sonay Kartal's dream week continued as she beat former Grand Slam champion Jelena Ostapenko at the Wuhan Open to reach the biggest final of her career. British number five Kartal is playing in only her third event since returning from a six-month absence with a back injury, but she now stands one more victory away from a WTA 1,000 title - one of the most prestigious prizes outside of the Grand Slams.

The 24-year-old's composure helped her secure a 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory in a pulsating semi-final against Latvia's Ostapenko. Kartal trailed 4-1 in both sets but remained level-headed and took advantage when Ostapenko stuttered in high-pressure moments.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev’s ranking points and prize money after Shanghai Masters semi-final loss
Racket.summary: Zverev was upset by Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in Shanghai. The post Alexander Zverev’s ranking points and prize money after Shanghai Masters semi-final loss appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexander Zverev was beaten 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 by world number 26 Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the Shanghai Masters semi-final on Saturday. Davidovich Fokina was broken just once and lost only six points on serve in the second set and three in the third. The Spaniard had won only one of his previous seven meetings with Zverev.

Zverev earned 400 ranking points, taking his total to 10,070, which leaves him 880 behind world number one Jannik Sinner. He also collected $340,190 in prize money. Davidovich Fokina will have the chance to earn $1,151,380 in the final, where he faces either Daniil Medvedev or Rafael Jodar.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev’s campaign at the 2026 Shanghai Masters is over after a surprise three-set semi-final loss to Alejandro Davidovich Fokina. The reigning French Open and US Open champion was upset 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 by world No 26 Davidovich Fokina at the Masters 1000 event on Saturday.

Davidovich Fokina was broken just once, and he lost only six points on his serve in the second set and just three in the third set. The 27-year-old Spaniard had won just one of the seven matches he had played against Zverev prior to this encounter.

Racket.title: Emma Raducanu 'will win Wimbledon one day' but US Open winner told to make key change
Racket.summary: Emma Raducanu 'will win Wimbledon one day' but US Open winner told to make key change Daily Mirror
bullets: Dan Evans has told The Telegraph he "genuinely" thinks Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon one day, while maintaining that she needs to spend more time on court. The former British No 1 said she appears unfazed in big matches and looks like she loves playing on Centre Court, which he described as a daunting place to play.

Raducanu, 23, won the US Open in 2021 but has not reached a Grand Slam quarter-final since. Her best Wimbledon result is the fourth round, reached twice, and last year she played Aryna Sabalenka on Centre Court. Injuries have affected her career and she has struggled to settle on a coach. Tim Henman has also said she can win another major, saying it comes down to process and daily work. Mark Petchey said last year it "won't be easy" but is possible if she changes her baseline game against big hitters.
Racket.copy:
Former British No 1 Dan Evans has claimed he "genuinely thinks Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon one day" - but maintained she needs to be on the court more often. The 23-year-old has been on our screens for half a decade having shot to stardom when she was just a teenager. Her stunning victory at the US Open in 2021 saw her profile skyrocket as she broke numerous records en route to claiming the top prize in New York.

That did bring with it huge expectation and Raducanu has not scaled those heights since. She's not even reached a Grand Slam quarter-final outside of her US Open success but Evans still sees her as talented enough to claim one of the sport's biggest honours.

Racket.title: Emma Raducanu: Retired Brit Dan Evans predicts former US Open champion 'will win Wimbledon' despite injuries and fitness issues
Racket.summary: Emma Raducanu: Retired Brit Dan Evans predicts former US Open champion 'will win Wimbledon' despite injuries and fitness issues Sky Sports
bullets: Former British No 1 Dan Evans has said he "genuinely" thinks Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon one day, despite her injury problems. Speaking to The Telegraph, he said she believes she is good and treats big matches as "just another match". Raducanu, 23, has not competed since losing the Queen's Club final to Donna Vekic in June, and a stress fracture in her lower right leg forced her to miss Wimbledon and the US Open.

Raducanu has dropped to world No 107, her lowest ranking in two years. Evans said she needs "a racket in her hand a bit more" and suggested endorsements may be pulling her in different directions, though he is told she trains hard for two to three hours with hardly any break. She was not named in Great Britain's Billie Jean King Cup Finals team in late September. After six months out she could use a protected ranking based on her top-50 position from the grass season.
Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu has dropped out of the world’s top 100 after missing Wimbledon and the US Open due to injury; You can watch the WTA Wuhan Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports.

Former British No 1 Dan Evans claims Emma Raducanu will add to her US Open triumph by winning Wimbledon - despite her recent injury woes. Raducanu has not competed since June, when she reached the Queen's Club final before losing to Donna Vekic.

Racket.title: 2026 Swiss Indoors Basel Entry List, Prize Money, Dates: Novak Djokovic, Ben Shelton headline
Racket.summary: All the key info ahead of a star-studded ATP 500 in Basel. The post 2026 Swiss Indoors Basel Entry List, Prize Money, Dates: Novak Djokovic, Ben Shelton headline appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Novak Djokovic will play the 2026 Swiss Indoors in Basel, the 55th edition of the indoor hard-court ATP 500 event, from 26 October to 1 November at the St. Jakobshalle. He accepted a wildcard for his fourth appearance and first since 2011, having won the title in 2009. Stan Wawrinka has also received a wildcard for what will be the final tournament of his career.

The 32-player singles draw has eight seeds, all in the top 20: Ben Shelton, Felix Auger-Aliassime, Arthur Fils, Djokovic, Taylor Fritz, Rafael Jodar, Alejandro Davidovich Fokina and Jiri Lehecka. Joao Fonseca is the defending champion after beating Davidovich Fokina in the 2025 final. Total prize money is €2,584,155, according to the ATP Tour website.
Racket.copy:
Novak Djokovic has made the surprise decision to compete at the 2026 Swiss Indoors, but who else will star at the tournament in Basel? This year’s Swiss Indoors will be the 55th edition of the indoor hard-court ATP 500 event, which is staged at the St. Jakobshalle in Basel.

Joao Fonseca is the reigning champion, having defeated Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the 2025 championship match. When will the 2026 Swiss Indoors be held? Main draw action at the 2026 Swiss Indoors will take place from 26 October to 1 November.

Racket.title: Daniil Medvedev gives ‘no comment’ answer at Shanghai Masters before Rafael Jodar clash
Racket.summary: Medvedev addressed a controversy after reaching the semi-finals in Shanghai. The post Daniil Medvedev gives ‘no comment’ answer at Shanghai Masters before Rafael Jodar clash appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Daniil Medvedev gave a "no comment" response when asked whether he would appeal the ranking points he lost after his Beijing disqualification. He was defaulted from his China Open semi-final against Novak Djokovic for accidentally hitting a fan with a ball, which stripped him of the 200 points he had earned. He beat Tommy Paul 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 in the Shanghai quarter-finals to set up a semi-final with Rafael Jodar.

Medvedev has a record of 11-1 on the Asian swing, having won the Hangzhou ATP 250 and reached the Beijing semi-finals. His 400 points in Shanghai lifted him from eighth to sixth in the Race to Turin. He is effectively fifth, as Jannik Sinner will miss the ATP Finals through injury, and holds a 540-point lead over Alex de Minaur in 10th.
Racket.copy:
Daniil Medvedev gave an intriguing response to a question about his Beijing disqualification after reaching the semi-finals at the 2026 Shanghai Masters. The former world No 1 defeated Tommy Paul 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 in the quarter-finals in Shanghai on Friday to set up a last four showdown with Rafael Jodar.

The 30-year-old Russian star’s run at the Masters 1000 tournament in Shanghai has been a continuation of his stellar form in China. Medvedev has amassed a 11-1 record during the 2026 Asian swing so far, having secured the title at the ATP 250 in Hangzhou and reached the semi-finals at the ATP 500 in Beijing prior to Shanghai.

Racket.title: Emma Raducanu ‘will win Wimbledon some day’, former British No 1 predicts
Racket.summary: Emma Raducanu ‘will win Wimbledon some day’, former British No 1 predicts The Independent
bullets: Former British No 1 Dan Evans has predicted Emma Raducanu "will win Wimbledon some day", telling The Telegraph that she plays big matches as though they are just another match. He said she needs to have a racket in her hand more, suggesting endorsements pull her in different directions, but has been told she is a good trainer who works two to three hours with hardly any break.

Raducanu won the US Open as an 18-year-old qualifier in 2021, her only title, and has reached the fourth round of a Grand Slam once since. She has dropped out of the world's top 100 after missing Wimbledon and the US Open with a stress fracture in her right leg. Evans, 36, retired at this year's Wimbledon after being denied a singles wildcard. He blamed Leon Smith, Great Britain's Davis Cup captain and the LTA's head of men's tennis, saying he was shown a lack of respect.
Racket.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Former British No 1 Dan Evans has confidently predicted that Emma Raducanu “will win Wimbledon some day”.

“She’s good, and I think – I’m saying this in as nice a way as possible – I think she thinks she’s good,” the now-retired Evans told The Telegraph in an interview. “Not in an arrogant way, but when she plays big matches, she’s like ‘Whatever. This is just another match.’ And yeah, I just think one day she’ll get it.”

Racket.title: Emma Raducanu tipped to win Wimbledon in bold call as ranking drops to two-year low
Racket.summary: Emma Raducanu tipped to win Wimbledon in bold call as ranking drops to two-year low AOL.com
bullets: Dan Evans, a former world No 21 and member of Britain's Davis Cup-winning squad in 2015, has told The Telegraph he "genuinely" thinks Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon one day. Racket.copy:
Dan Evans has sensationally claimed that Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon - despite her recent injury woes. Raducanu has been sidelined by a leg injury since June and pulled out of her home Slam on the eve of the tournament. After spending four months on the sidelines, the Brit has dropped to No. 107 in the world, her worst ranking in two years. But Evans, a former world No. 21 who was part of Britain's Davis Cup-winning squad in 2015, still believes that Raducanu has what it takes to lift the Venus Rosewater Dish.

Racket.title: Daniil Medvedev sends clear message to Rafael Jodar at Shanghai Masters
Racket.summary: Medvedev made a comment involving Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer. The post Daniil Medvedev sends clear message to Rafael Jodar at Shanghai Masters appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Daniil Medvedev, the world number five, will face world number 13 Rafael Jodar in the Shanghai Masters semi-finals, their first meeting. Medvedev beat Tommy Paul 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 in the quarter-finals, while Jodar defeated Casper Ruud 4-6, 6-4, 6-3. Medvedev said he saved three break points in the opening game of the second set against Paul but was broken, before stepping up on serve in the third.

Looking ahead, Medvedev referred to Roger Federer, Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal, saying players adapt somewhat when they meet often. He said Djokovic plays largely the same tennis throughout the year. He said that on a fast court the match comes down to breaking serve and being strong on one's own, and he expects a tough match.
Racket.copy:
Daniil Medvedev made a comment about Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer as he looked ahead to his clash with Rafael Jodar at the 2026 Shanghai Masters. World No 5 Medvedev will face world No 13 Jodar in the semi-finals at the Masters 1000 tournament in Shanghai. It will be the pair’s first encounter.

The 2021 US Open champion and former world No 1 earned a 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 victory over Tommy Paul in the Shanghai quarter-finals on Friday after Jodar defeated Casper Ruud 4-6, 6-4, 6-3.

Racket.title: Dan Evans interview: Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon
Racket.summary: Dan Evans interview: Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon The Telegraph
bullets: Dan Evans has told The Telegraph, in an interview at Robin Hood Golf Club in Solihull, that he "genuinely" thinks Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon one day. He said she is good and thinks she is good, and that in big matches she treats each one as "just another match".

Evans said the crowd plays a big part in tennis and that Centre Court is a daunting place to play, but that Raducanu looks like she loves it. He added that she needs a racket in her hand a bit more, with endorsements pulling her in different directions, though he is told she trains for two to three hours with hardly any break. The interview notes his verdict may seem ambitious after a season in which injuries forced her to miss more matches than she played.
Racket.copy:
There we are, sitting in the clubhouse of Solihull’s Robin Hood Golf Club, when Dan Evans comes out with a true marmalade-dropper about Emma Raducanu. “I genuinely think she will win Wimbledon one day.”

“Well, that’s a headline,” I reply, trying not to spill my lime and soda. “Yeah, I don’t know why,” Evans says with a crooked grin. “She’s good, and I think – I’m saying this in as nice a way as possible – I think she thinks she’s good. Not in an arrogant way, but when she plays big matches, she’s like ‘Whatever. This is just another match.’ And yeah, I just think one day she’ll get it.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: ‘We Don’t Want to Stop Here’
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: ‘We Don’t Want to Stop Here’ BWF World Tour
bullets: Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan became the first Malaysian women's doubles pair to reach the semi-finals of the Denmark Open in 18 years. They beat Treesa Jolly/Gayatri Gopichand Pullela 14-21 21-17 21-11 in the quarter-finals of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026. Chin Eei Hui/Wong Pei Tty were the last Malaysians to do so, winning the title in 2008, which remains the country's only women's doubles success at the tournament.

Tan said the pair had been too defensive and careful early on, and talked on court when trailing 14-11, telling each other to enjoy every point. Thinaah described the year as a rollercoaster and called the semi-final a positive step. They next face Bao Li Jing/Cao Zo Han in a first meeting, an emerging partnership Thinaah expects to be a stern test.
Racket.copy:
Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan have ended an 18-year wait for a Malaysian women’s doubles semifinalists at the Denmark Open but the history makers have no intention of stopping there.

Racket.title: How much does a coach get paid by the biggest names in tennis? All is revealed
Racket.summary: Greg Rusedski reveals how much a top tennis coach is paid. The post How much does a coach get paid by the biggest names in tennis? All is revealed appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Former British No 1 Greg Rusedski said on his podcast that there is no set formula for paying a tennis coach, with the arrangement negotiated between agent, player and coach. Most coaches receive a retainer plus bonuses and a guaranteed annual amount. Weekly fees range from $2,000 to as much as $25,000 including bonuses. Some coaches take a percentage of prize money, typically 5–10% from the second round, or only from the quarter-finals, semi-finals, finals or title wins if the base is higher.

Rusedski cited Brad Gilbert, who he said took only a percentage of prize money, with expenses paid and a higher percentage at the Grand Slams. He noted that prize money has risen sharply, with players on 15–23 records at the Shanghai Masters earning $1.3m. The piece notes Ivan Ljubicic's tie-up with Felix Auger-Aliassime and that Juan Carlos Ferrero will return in 2027 after splitting with Carlos Alcaraz last December.
Racket.copy:
How much is a tennis coach paid and how do the world’s leading players hand out bonuses? It is an area of the sport few outside of the tennis bubble get any insight on, so the comments from former British No 1 Greg Rusedski on the latest edition of his podcast made for fascinating viewing.

Rusedski, a former world No 4 who reached the US Open final in 1997, worked with French player Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard on a brief trial that came to an end after Wimbledon in June and he has also worked with former world No 1 Victoria Azarenka.

Former Australian Open champion Keys said his body could never move like that, citing the way he slides into corners, stops and cuts. bullets: Greg Rusedski believes it is a "smart play" for Emma Raducanu to delay her return from a stress fracture, which has kept her off the WTA Tour since Queen's Club in June. Her ranking was 31 when she was injured and she has since dropped out of the top 100. If she stays off the circuit until at least January, passing the six-month injury threshold, she would be eligible for a protected ranking.

That ranking would allow her to enter up to eight tournaments in a season, including a maximum of two Grand Slams, though she would not be seeded at the Australian Open. Rusedski said an extended off-season would help her hit the ground running in 2027, and that staying healthy is her main challenge. He contrasted her rise, winning the 2021 US Open as an 18-year-old qualifier, with the steadier climb of 21-year-old Alex Eala, who has moved from 50 to the top 20 this year.
Racket.copy:

Since a hectic final weekend at Queen’s Club in June, Raducanu has not played a single match on the WTA Tour due to her ongoing injury. The former US Open champion has posted videos of herself in training in the past few weeks, but it remains to be seen if she will play another tournament this year.

Despite dropping out of the top 100, Raducanu will be eligible for a protected ranking if she stays off the circuit until at least January, which will take her past the six-month injury threshold.

During the 20-year-old’s three-set win, he shouted, “Dame la puta toalla, cono!” (“Give me the f****** towel, damn it!”) to a ball kid. Pinoargote picked up on this and hit the Spaniard with a code violation for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Racket.title: $350 million to a new Tour structure: 6 key takeaways from ATP’s seismic OneVision plans
Racket.summary: This will change men's tennis in a huge way! The post $350 million to a new Tour structure: 6 key takeaways from ATP’s seismic OneVision plans appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi has unveiled OneVision proposals, intended for the 2028 season subject to consultation and approval, to alter prize money distribution, reduce pressure to overplay and give players more choice over where and when to compete. The Masters 1000 Bonus Pool would rise from $21.5m to $50m, with payments tied to rankings at each mandatory Masters 1000, and players would need to compete in at least four to qualify.

The ATP plans to invest $105m annually in central player compensation from 2028, including $25m for career support for year-end top 250 players and $30m for pension contributions. Total player compensation, excluding Grand Slams, is estimated to reach $350m from 2028. The proposals also seek dedicated calendar weeks for each tournament level, including the tenth Masters 1000 in Saudi Arabia from 2028, and a rankings reform giving more weight to the biggest events.
Racket.copy:
ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi has released bold proposals that will try to grow tennis and alter prize money distribution, reduce the pressure to “overplay”, and give players the choice of where and when to compete.

The tennis body has unveiled plans for OneVision, which is mooted to be in place for the 2028 season, subject to further consultation and approval. 2026 has been a year dominated by injuries, most notably to world No 1 Jannik Sinner and the youngest-ever player to complete the career Grand Slam, Carlos Alcaraz. Now, it seems like tennis authorities want to try to do something to fix that.

Racket.copy:
More than the archetypal badminton player, Jagsher Singh Khangurra has the bearing of a mild-mannered chess talent: studious, understated. In the men’s singles quarterfinals of the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 on Thursday, facing an explosive opponent in Jhuang Yuan-Syue, Khangurra produced a performance as finely crafted and cerebral as befits an accomplished chess player. Racket.title: Stefan Milicevic given 24-year ban for match-fixing: Serbian player, 29, banned from tennis until 2050
Racket.summary: Stefan Milicevic given 24-year ban for match-fixing: Serbian player, 29, banned from tennis until 2050 Sky Sports
bullets: Serbian player Stefan Milicevic has been banned for 24 years for match-fixing after the International Tennis Integrity Agency found he led a "corrupt network" between 2022 and 2024. The 29-year-old, whose highest ranking was 1338, fixed six matches, five of which he played in, and attempted to fix six more. He was also fined $70,000 (£52,800).

The ITIA said Milicevic did not engage or co-operate with the investigation. His suspension ends on 8 October 2050, when he will be 53. While suspended he cannot play in, coach at or attend events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, the WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams or any national association.
Racket.copy:
A Serbian tennis player has been handed a massive 24-year ban for match-fixing. Stefan Milicevic led a "corrupt network" of match-fixing between 2022 and 2024, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), with the 29-year-old shown to have fixed six matches - five of which he played in - and attempted to with six more.

Milicevic, whose highest ATP ranking was 1338, did not engage or co-operate with the investigation, according to the ITIA, and was also fined 70,000 US dollars (£52,800). The ITIA's statement on Thursday said: "Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network during the same period, resulting in a number of other players fixing matches."

Racket.title: Serb player banned until 2050 for tennis match-fixing

bullets: Serbian player Stefan Milicevic has been given a 24-year suspension from tennis for match-fixing, one of the most severe punishments outside a lifetime ban. The International Tennis Integrity Authority said he was also charged with recruiting, or attempting to recruit, multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network. The severity of the sanction is partly due to his lack of co-operation, as he did not engage despite seven attempts to contact him. bullets: The University of Maryland has indefinitely suspended its club tennis team after a graphic featuring Ku Klux Klan imagery, in an altered Maryland state flag, was circulated to other universities in a shared Google document before a regional tournament. Toni Rachal, president of Howard University's club tennis team, spotted it, and Howard's club questioned how it reached official tournament materials.

The suspension is pending an administrative investigation by the office of student conduct, and the university police and civil rights office have also opened investigations. Maryland withdrew from the tournament and forfeited its matches, while Howard reached the semi-finals, its best result in the event since the club was established in 2021. University president Darryll J Pines said only a few members may have been directly involved, while Black student union leaders said the incident was not isolated.
Racket.copy:

The controversy erupted after Toni Rachal, president of Howard University’s club tennis team, spotted the offensive material in a shared Google document sent to participating schools before last weekend’s tournament, WUSA9 reported.

Racket.title: Finding Renée Richards: the complicated past and present of a trans sports pioneer
Racket.summary: In 1977, Richards sued to play in the US Open after transitioning. Now she supports bans on trans athletes in women’s sports. A new biography explores a complex legacy It was a story that dominated tennis headlines back in 1977: Dr Renée Richards, an ophthalmologist who excelled as a male amateur player before a sex-change operation, was suing for the right to play in the women’s draw of the US Open. Where did Richards go for legal assistance? None other than Roy Cohn. Better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump, Cohn turned his attention to fighting for Richards’s inclusion. His firm successfully argued the case – part of the narrative of a new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman. Continue reading...
bullets: A new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis's Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman, revisits the 1977 lawsuit in which Richards, an ophthalmologist who had played as a male amateur before a sex-change operation, sued for the right to play in the women's US Open draw. Roy Cohn's firm successfully argued the case, though the decision was limited to Richards and set no precedent for other trans people.

Kliegman, a trans and non-binary sports journalist, drew on Richards' autobiographies, interview transcripts from an unpublished memoir and several in-person interviews with Richards, now 92. Kliegman said Richards now believes trans women and girls should not play women's sports unless they have not undergone male puberty, a reversal of her 1977 position that created tension between them. At Richards' wish, the book uses her former name and he/him pronouns for her early life.
Racket.copy:
It was a story that dominated tennis headlines back in 1977: Dr Renée Richards, an ophthalmologist who excelled as a male amateur player before a sex-change operation, was suing for the right to play in the women’s draw of the US Open. Where did Richards go for legal assistance? None other than Roy Cohn.

Better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump, Cohn turned his attention to fighting for Richards’s inclusion. His firm successfully argued the case – part of the narrative of a new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman.

Racket.summary: Sonay Kartal upsets Swiss ninth seed Belinda Bencic to reach the Wuhan Open third round as she continues to build momentum.
bullets: Britain's Sonay Kartal beat ninth seed Belinda Bencic 6-0 7-5 in the second round of the Wuhan Open, the second biggest win of her career by ranking. The 24-year-old reached a career-high ranking of 44 last year but has slipped to 170th after a six-month injury absence, while Bencic is world number 12 and was a Wimbledon semi-finalist last year.

Kartal suffered a stress fracture in her back in March, missing three of this year's four Grand Slams, including Wimbledon. She has won four of five matches since returning, having reached the third round in Beijing and beaten Anhelina Kalinina in her Wuhan opener. She said she trusted her level would return but that sustaining it would be the hardest challenge, and she next faces Jasmine Paolini or Nikola Bartunkova.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal upset ninth seed Belinda Bencic as she continued to build post-injury momentum at the Wuhan Open. Kartal reached a career-high ranking of 44 last year but has slipped to 170th in the world after a six-month injury absence.

Having returned to action for Great Britain at last month's Billie Jean King Cup Finals, the 24-year-old reached the third round at the Beijing Open last week before beating Ukraine's Anhelina Kalinina in her opening match in Wuhan.

Racket.title: 2026 WTA Finals: The 7 women who have qualified as Karolina Muchova, Iga Swiatek, Iva Jovic battle for final spot
Racket.summary: Seven of the eight places for the WTA Finals have been confirmed. The post 2026 WTA Finals: The 7 women who have qualified as Karolina Muchova, Iga Swiatek, Iva Jovic battle for final spot appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Seven players have qualified for the eight-player WTA Finals at Indian Wells: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff, Linda Noskova and Elina Svitolina. Svitolina moved past the projected cut-off with her second-round win at the Wuhan Open, although the WTA has yet to confirm her place or those of Pegula and Gauff, who are mathematically assured.

Muchova and Swiatek are the main candidates for the last place, with Marta Kostyuk all but out after her second-round defeat in Wuhan and Iva Jovic an outside chance. Reigning world No 1 Rybakina was first to qualify, having won last year's event undefeated. Noskova qualified as the highest-ranked current-year Grand Slam winner after her Wimbledon title, despite being eighth in the race.
Racket.copy:
Only one ticket remains in the WTA Rankings Race To Indian Wells with Elina Svitolina the latest to secure her place at the season-ending tournament. Although the WTA has yet to officially confirm that Svitolina has punched her ticket to the lucrative event, the Ukrainian moved ahead of the projected cut-off mark with her second-round win at the Wuhan Open.

That leaves only one spot open for the eight-player tournament in the United States, with Karolina Muchova, Marta Kostyuk, Iga Swiatek and Iva Jovic still in the hunt. Kostyuk’s second-round defeat in Wuhan means she is all but out of the race, while Jovic has an outside chance as she is well adrift, leaving Muchova and Swiatek as the two main candidates, although the latter has some ground to make up.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: Straight Off the Road, Li Rocks Pusarla
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: Straight Off the Road, Li Rocks Pusarla BWF World Tour
bullets: Germany's Yvonne Li, ranked 45th in the world, beat India's Pusarla V. Sindhu 13-21 25-23 21-19 in 65 minutes in the first round of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 in Odense. Li was promoted from the reserves list into the main draw late on Monday evening and drove three hours from Hamburg on the morning of the match.

Li said she slowed the tempo and found variation from the front court so Sindhu could not attack easily. Sindhu said her disappointment was about her unforced errors rather than the length of the match. Li won the Dutch Open in September and reached the second round of last week's Arctic Open. She credited a change of training environment two years ago, after the Olympics, and said her coach now travels with her more. She next faces India's Tanvi Sharma, who beat Natsuki Nidaira 21-17 16-21 21-19.
Racket.copy:
Yvonne Li’s day began with a message and a decision. Late on Monday evening, she was informed she had been promoted from the reserves list into the main draw of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026. By sunrise, she was in her car, making the three-hour journey from Hamburg to Odense. A few hours later, she was standing on Court 2 having pulled off one of the biggest results of the opening round – the world No.45 stunned Pusarla V. Sindhu 13-21 25-23 21-19 in a 65-minute thriller.

“I got the message last night and drove to Odense this morning,” Li said. “After a three-hour drive, I just played. I can’t really believe it.” After being outplayed in the opening game, Li gradually wrestled control from the Indian shuttler. She found greater variation at the net and slowed the tempo at crucial moments, forcing Pusarla out of her comfort zone.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: Gemke Knocks Out Vitidsarn
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: Gemke Knocks Out Vitidsarn BWF World Tour
bullets: Rasmus Gemke, the world No.27, beat top seed and world No.1 Kunlavut Vitidsarn 13-21 21-17 21-12 in the first round of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026, coming back from a game down. The 29-year-old said it was a fantastic feeling to win against the world No.1 on home soil in front of the crowd, and described the atmosphere as amazing.

Gemke admitted he initially struggled to find his rhythm and the quality needed to challenge Vitidsarn, but fought back as the Thai player made errors. He called the result a big confidence boost. It was not his first win over the recent Asian Games gold medallist this season, as he also beat him in three games at the China Open in July. Gemke will next play the winner of the match between Ng Ka Long Angus and Yushi Tanaka.
Racket.copy:
Rasmus Gemke delivered one of the biggest surprises of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 first round, coming from a game down to defeat top seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn 13-21 21-17 21-12.

“Fantastic feeling winning against the world No.1 on home soil in front of these spectators. The atmosphere was amazing and I’m just really happy and proud,” Gemke said. Gemke admitted initially struggling to find his rhythm and produce the quality needed to challenge the Thai star. Despite that, the world No.27 refused to give up.

Racket.title: World Juniors: Mady Sow Stays on Track
Racket.summary: World Juniors: Mady Sow Stays on Track BWF
bullets: Top seed Mady Sow of France came from a game down to beat Japan's Daiki Masuda 12-15 15-11 15-11 in the third round of the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026. The 16-year-old left-hander, who stands 190cm, said he was shocked to lose the first game and that his goal was to play every point at 100 per cent.

This is Sow's second World Junior Championships and his first as favourite in men's singles. He arrived in Cairo as European junior champion and Badminton Europe Young Player of the Year. He said he hopes to win a medal for himself and the French team. France has had a strong year, with silver at the Thomas Cup and two gold medals at the World Championships, and Sow said watching team-mate Alex Lanier win medals pushed him to train harder.
Racket.copy:
For a fair part of his third round match at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026, Mady Sow looked vulnerable. The European junior champion, who has been among the most talked-about emerging players over the past two years, flirted with danger before recovering to keep himself in the contest against Japan’s Daiki Masuda.

“First of all, I was shocked because I didn’t expect to lose the first game,” the top seed said, after completing the 12-15 15-11 15-11 win. “He played very well. So for me, my goal was to play 100 per cent every point.

Racket.title: Coco Gauff abuse leads Andy Roddick to make ‘disgustingly racist filth’ comment
Racket.summary: "This is disgusting. It has to stop." The post Coco Gauff abuse leads Andy Roddick to make ‘disgustingly racist filth’ comment appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Andy Roddick called the racist abuse Coco Gauff received during the China Open "disgusting" on his Served podcast. Gauff was targeted on social media after a video review incident in her 7-5, 6-1 third-round win over 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Xinran Sun in Beijing.

Gauff wrote that people could dislike her or disagree with what happened without being racist, adding that she is not a cheater or a thief. After losing 6-3, 6-3 to Elise Mertens in the fourth round, she called the abuse draining and said she turns off her phone. Roddick said Gauff did nothing wrong, described her as one of the most high-character people, and said the abuse has to stop.
Racket.copy:
Andy Roddick has described the abuse Coco Gauff received during the 2026 China Open as “disgusting” as he hailed the American star’s character. Gauff was the target of racist abuse on social media following a video review incident during her 7-5, 6-1 third round win against 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Xinran Sun in Beijing.

In response to a racist comment directed at her on X/Twitter, Gauff wrote: “Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist. “The amount of racist comments/dms I’ve received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I’m not a cheater or a thief.”

Racket.title: Will the Six Kings Slam go ahead? Withdrawal of one player could end the richest event in tennis
Racket.summary: Alcaraz and Djokovic have yet to confirm if they will play in Saudi Arabia after terror attacks. The post Will the Six Kings Slam go ahead? Withdrawal of one player could end the richest event in tennis appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: This year's Six Kings Slam in Riyadh, due to start on 21 October, is in doubt after militants struck King Khalid International Airport, killing at least 12 people and injuring more than 300. The attacks were claimed by Yemen's Houthi movement, and a NOTAM says the airport remains closed until 21:00 GMT on Saturday, 17 October.

Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien are scheduled to play, each with a $1.5m appearance fee. Governments are advising foreign tourists against travelling to Riyadh, and the Alcaraz, Djokovic and Zverev camps have not commented. Andy Roddick said on his Served podcast that he would not go, as it is an exhibition and the payday would not offset the risk.
Racket.copy:
The countdown is on to the richest event in tennis, but there has to be a huge cloud of uncertainty hanging over this year’s Six Kings Slam. Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien are all scheduled to play in an exhibition event in Saudi Arabia that offers a $1.5 million appearance fee for each competitor.

That money could be collected from playing just one best-of-three-set match in Riyadh, but the challenge for event organisers this year is the current security issue in the host city.

Racket.title: Will Carlos Alcaraz’s ‘protest’ against the ATP Tour turn into a full scale revolt?
Racket.summary: Alcaraz is not happy with extended Masters 1000 tournaments - will he skip playing in 2027? The post Will Carlos Alcaraz’s ‘protest’ against the ATP Tour turn into a full scale revolt? appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz has expressed frustration at the number of mandatory events on the ATP Tour and may follow through on a threat to miss key tournaments in 2027. He won the ATP 500 title in Tokyo days after the Laver Cup in London, and has suggested he would skip parts of next season to avoid a repeat of the wrist injury that followed the Barcelona Open in April and kept him out until mid-August.

Masters 1000 events are mandatory for top players, carry no appearance fees and now run for 12 days. Tim Henman told Tennis365 the format is too much tennis and should be cut to eight or nine days, while Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev have made similar claims. Alcaraz is reportedly declining some ATP Tour media team requests as a 'mini protest' and could face financial penalties for skipping events when fit.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz has expressed his frustration at the number of mandatory events on the ATP Tour and he may now follow through with his threat to miss key events in 2027. Alcaraz won the ATP 500 title in Tokyo last week and appeared to enjoy his time on court at an event he opted to play despite the quick turnaround from the Laver Cup in London a few days earlier.

While a player who has already collected over $66 million in career prize money is not likely to be entirely focused on money at this point in his career, Alcaraz would have been paid a big fee for his appearance in Tokyo.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev on the cusp of equalling Carlos Alcaraz’s Masters record after latest win
Racket.summary: He'd edging closer... The post Alexander Zverev on the cusp of equalling Carlos Alcaraz’s Masters record after latest win appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexander Zverev reached the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals by beating Alexander Bublik in three sets, needing two tie-breaks against the world No 18. The German, who has just been confirmed as year-end world No 1, took a fall in his opening match against Wu Yibing, and his ankle appeared to trouble him again. Novak Djokovic, Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz are among the top seeds already out.

Zverev has won Masters titles at five different events: Madrid, Rome, Canada, Cincinnati and Paris. A Shanghai title would put him level with Alcaraz on that measure. He plays Alex de Minaur next, having won eight of their 12 meetings, though he has lost the last two. Daniil Medvedev and Felix Auger-Aliassime are the only other top-10 players left, both in the other half of the draw.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev came through a difficult test against Alexander Bublik to confirm his place in the quarterfinals of the Shanghai Masters. Zverev, who has just been confirmed as the year-end world No 1, needed three sets to defeat Bublik in what was a very competitive match on the Masters tournament’s main court.

The German needed two tie-breaks to topple Bublik, but he did not look entirely comfortably against the world No 18. Zverev took a fall in his opening round match against Wu Yibing and his ankle appeared to be troubling him again in his fourth round match.

Racket.title: ‘A kind of death’ – ATP veteran opens up on painful reality of being ‘past his prime’
Racket.summary: The Frenchman doesn't want to retire just yet. The post ‘A kind of death’ – ATP veteran opens up on painful reality of being ‘past his prime’ appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Adrian Mannarino, 38 and ranked 78th, has no plans to retire but admits it is hard to accept that he is "past his prime". The Frenchman beat sixth seed Flavio Cobolli in the second round of the Shanghai Masters. His best year came in 2023, when he finished ranked 22nd with three ATP Tour titles and three top-10 wins.

Speaking to L'Equipe, Mannarino said he knows he will never be as fast or as enduring as before, calling that "a kind of death" for a tennis player. He said he still enjoys the sport and that it pays very well, and he may play another year or two. The five-time tour title winner, who has earned over $15m in prize money, said that cutting training intensity quickly hurts his results.
Racket.copy:
Adrian Mannarino has no plans to retire just yet, but the veteran admits it is hard to accept that he is “past his prime”. The 38-year-old currently sits at 78th in the world and is more than capable of pulling off an upset, something he did in his second-round win over sixth seed Flavio Cobolli at the Shanghai Masters.

The Frenchman had the best year of his career at the age of 35 when he finished 2023 with a year-end ranking of 22, which included three ATP Tour titles and three top 10 victories.

Racket.title: Inside Wuhan: How the city at the heart of a global pandemic is fighting back
Racket.summary: Tennis365 visits Wuhan and sees a different side to the city. The post Inside Wuhan: How the city at the heart of a global pandemic is fighting back appeared first on Tennis365 .
Racket.copy:
The 2026 Wuhan Open is underway, with a city that became infamous for all the wrong reasons at the turn of the decade eager to put on a show that changes a few negative perceptions.

Tennis365 were invited to attend the tournament in Wuhan last year and our experience was a real opener for all the right reasons, as we experienced incredible hospitality, a warm welcome from the locals and left with a very different view of a city that may never fully recover from it’s status as the starting point for the world’s biggest pandemic.

Racket.title: Jannik Sinner urged to follow Rafael Nadal’s example amid growing injury concerns
Racket.summary: Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have opted for a similar strategy. The post Jannik Sinner urged to follow Rafael Nadal’s example amid growing injury concerns appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Tennis analyst Gill Gross has urged Jannik Sinner to be more transparent about the knee injury that has ended his season, saying in an Instagram video that he sees little downside to doing so. Sinner, 25, beat Alexander Zverev in four sets to defend his Wimbledon title in mid-July and is not expected to play again until 2027.

Gross contrasted Sinner with Rafael Nadal, who regularly gave fans detailed injury updates, and said openness would help stop speculation. Little has been disclosed about Carlos Alcaraz's wrist injury either. Separately, Rick Macci, Serena Williams' former coach, dismissed talk that Sinner is serving a "silent" doping ban. Such talk likely stems from his three-month ban in 2025 after twice testing positive for clostebol in March 2024. Sinner's entourage appears content with its current strategy.
Racket.copy:
Jannik Sinner has been urged to be more “transparent” about the knee injury that prematurely ended his season. When Sinner defended his Wimbledon title after beating Alexander Zverev in four sets in mid-July, very few would have predicted he wouldn’t play again until 2027.

The 25-year-old has struggled with his injury under wraps. While Rafael Nadal used to provide regular updates on his injuries over the years, tennis fans have not been told a great deal about Alcaraz’s wrist injury and Sinner’s current issue.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev issues telling injury update after Shanghai Masters scare
Racket.summary: "I'm starting to feel my body more and more." The post Alexander Zverev issues telling injury update after Shanghai Masters scare appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexander Zverev beat world No 22 Alexander Bublik 7-6(6), 4-6, 7-6(1) in the Shanghai Masters last 16 on Tuesday, despite appearing to be in discomfort. The world No 2 saved four set points and recovered from 3-6 down in the first-set tiebreak. After losing serve in the opening game of the decider, he broke straight back to love.

The 29-year-old had an ankle problem during earlier wins over Wu Yibing and Quentin Halys. He told Tennis TV it was "acting up, unfortunately, again", which he called understandable given how much he has played. He described becoming world No 1 for the first time later this year as special, bringing a sense of responsibility, particularly as he is close to 30. He meets world No 9 Alex de Minaur in the quarter-finals.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev provided an injury update after he appeared to be in discomfort during his fourth round win at the 2026 Shanghai Masters. The two-time Grand Slam champion prevailed 7-6(6), 4-6, 7-6(1) against world No 22 Alexander Bublik in a pulsating last 16 clash in Shanghai on Tuesday.

World No 2 Zverev fought off four set points and recovered from a 3-6 deficit in the tiebreak to sneak through the first set. After Bublik earned the only break of the second set en route to levelling the match, Zverev found himself in trouble when he lost serve again in the opening game of the final set.

Racket.title: Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open
Racket.summary: Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open Sky Sports
bullets: Alexander Zverev beat Alexander Bublik 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) to reach the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals, in his first match since clinching the year-end world No 1 ranking for the first time on Monday. The French Open and US Open champion admitted his ankle was "acting up". He next plays ninth seed Alex de Minaur, who beat Karen Khachanov 6-3 6-4.

Current world No 1 Jannik Sinner is out for the rest of 2026 with a knee injury, and Carlos Alcaraz cannot overtake Zverev this year. Zverev said finishing as world No 1 brings a different responsibility. Elsewhere, Katie Boulter lost 6-3 6-1 to 11th seed Diana Shnaider in the Wuhan Open first round. Iga Swiatek is 10th in the qualifying table for the WTA Finals (8-15 November, Indian Wells), with four of the eight spots still available.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters. Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open this year, never looked 100 per cent comfortable, and admitted his "ankle was acting up" following his win.

The top seed will take on ninth seed Alex de Minaur next after the Australian produced one of his best performances of the year to beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets 6-3 6-4 to advance.

Racket.title: Rafael Nadal hits back at claims he’s heard about Carlos Alcaraz recently – ‘Makes no sense’
Racket.summary: Nadal is against what people are saying about Carlos Alcaraz. The post Rafael Nadal hits back at claims he’s heard about Carlos Alcaraz recently – ‘Makes no sense’ appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Rafael Nadal has rejected the description of Carlos Alcaraz as a "prospect", following Alcaraz's exit from the Shanghai Masters. As reported by Kalshi Tennis, Nadal said that with seven Grand Slams Alcaraz is not just a promise for the future but already a legend, noting few players in history have won seven. Nadal partnered Alcaraz in doubles at the Paris Olympics.

Alcaraz, 23, has more Grand Slam titles than Stefan Edberg and Boris Becker, and the same number as Mats Wilander and John McEnroe. He became the youngest player to complete the Career Grand Slam earlier this year by winning the Australian Open for the first time, and has finished as year-end world No 1 twice. He has yet to win the Paris Masters or the ATP Finals.
Racket.copy:
In many ways, Carlos Alcaraz took the torch from Rafael Nadal when he retired from the sport in 2024. Nadal dominated the Spanish tennis landscape for nearly two decades before Alcaraz arrived as a fresh-faced tennis towards the end of the 2010s.

As Nadal’s playing career was coming to an end, Alcaraz began to make a name for himself on the ATP Tour. He was a four-time Grand Slam winner by the time the Spaniard called time on his playing career.

Ever dreamed of following in the footsteps of some of the world’s greatest tennis stars? Racket.title: Italian media reveal Jannik Sinner’s injury treatment plan under supervision of renowned specialist
Racket.summary: "We are sure that even Jannik, number one in the world, in the coming months will recover well." The post Italian media reveal Jannik Sinner’s injury treatment plan under supervision of renowned specialist appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Jannik Sinner has started treatment on his injured knee, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The world No 1 has been absent from the ATP Tour since Wimbledon and announced last week that his 2026 season was over, so he will not return before 2027. He has already received platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment from Lyon-based orthopaedic surgeon Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet, who has operated on several Juventus players and examined Kylian Mbappe's knee.

Rehabilitation will be run through the Physioclinic centre under its co-founder Dr Herbert Schoenhuber, who helped Italian skier Sofia Goggia recover for the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, where she won silver. The connection comes through the friendship between Sinner's agent, Alex Vittur, and skier Alberto Tomba, whom Schoenhuber has also treated. Most physiotherapy and training will take place in Monte Carlo, with a return in Australia early in 2027 if all goes to plan.
Racket.copy:
Jannik Sinner has started treatment on his injured knee with Italian media confirming he will be treated by a renowned sports medicine specialist. The reigning world No 1 has been absent from the ATP Tour since Wimbledon due to a knee injury and he won’t return to action before 2027 as he announced last week that the “2026 season is officially over” as reveal “I need to think about my long-term career”.

Sinner and his team have given very little away about the full extent of his injury, but more information has now emerged about the rehabilitation plan for the coming months. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the five-time Grand Slam winner has already received Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) treatment by Lyon-based orthopaedic surgeon Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet – who has operated on several Juventus players in recent months while he also examined French and Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe’s injured knee.

The HSBC Championships at The Queen’s Club is set to return in 2027 with tickets for the women’s and men’s tournaments going on sale in November. Taking place from 5-20 June, be part of the next chapter in tennis history as British favourites and global stars battle for HSBC Championships glory.

Racket.title: ‘Alex Eala will be fine – but she needs to make a big change after shock Wuhan Open loss’
Racket.summary: A legendary coach has shared his thoughts after Alex Eala's defeat in Wuhan. The post ‘Alex Eala will be fine – but she needs to make a big change after shock Wuhan Open loss’ appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alex Eala, the world No 19 and 13th seed, lost 4-6, 6-3, 6-3 to 217th-ranked qualifier Shi Han in the opening round of the WTA 1000 Wuhan Open on Monday. The 21-year-old led 6-4, 3-2 but lost the next seven games and fell 0-3 down in the decider. It was her first match since losing to Wang Xiyu in the Asian Games semi-finals.

Coach Rick Macci, a former coach of Serena and Venus Williams, said on X that Eala "will be fine" and has many of the boxes checked for a top-ten player, but that her serve needs "reconstructive surgery". Golf.title: All the players who have left LIV Golf (so far)
Golf.summary: All the players who have left LIV Golf (so far) Golf Digest
bullets: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September. Its future as "LIV Golf 2.0" depends on key stakeholder and court approval for a transaction with angel investor BC Partners, and on the commitment of top players who would be equity owners under CEO Scott O'Neil's plan. Brooks Koepka left on 23 December 2025 and Patrick Reed made his exit official on 28 January 2026. Sergio Garcia's contract was terminated at a New Jersey hearing on 6 October.

Jon Rahm's lawyer told the judge on 7 October that his client had "no interest" in LIV 2.0, and David Puig said he does not see himself playing in it. Abraham Ancer, Charles Howell III and Thomas Pieters are reported to be heading to the DP World Tour, and Adrian Meronk is reported to have no intention of extending his contract. Cameron Smith is among players seeking a release similar to Garcia's, and LIV has asked for an extra week to review his request.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf 1.0 is gone. The pomp, pageantry and hot-air-balloon contracts of the LIV’s first iteration went up in smoke when the league filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September. Now the future of LIV Golf hinges on financing efforts for its next chapter, colloquially referred to as LIV Golf 2.0. According to recent reports, the league must obtain key stakeholder and court approval to complete the transaction with its angel investor, BC Partners.

Key to the future of LIV Golf, however, is the status of its top pros, who will operate as equity owners of the league and its respective teams under the plan laid out by CEO Scott O’Neil. Without those players and their literal and figurative buy-in, LIV Golf may not survive to see its second chapter. So where does that leave the floundering tour as the clock continues to tick? Which players have indicated their intention of leaving (or have formally asked the court to be released from their 1.0 contract), which haven’t and which are still sitting on the fence? Let’s take a look.

Golf.title: Rahm reaches deal over LIV Golf exit

bullets: Jon Rahm has reached a separation agreement with LIV Golf, according to bankruptcy court documents filed on Wednesday. The deal followed his lawyer telling US Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey Judge Michael Kaplan last week that Rahm would not return to LIV under the proposed new financial plans. Kaplan must approve the agreement next month.

Rahm, 31, was LIV's largest unsecured creditor, owed $7.5m when it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy last month, and was thought to be owed much more after a reported $300m deal signed in December 2023. He will keep his image and likeness, plus the "Rahmbo" and "Legion XIII" brands, provided the team name is not used in another league. LIV keeps rights for historical context. He won the 2026 LIV season crown, his third in a row.

bullets: The National Park Service felled at least 400 trees at East Potomac golf course last weekend, in open defiance of a federal court order that severely limited tree removal. Golf.copy:
“I had friends who would tell me they’re into gardening,” Donald Trump told me. This was years before his first term as president, and the subject was one of his recurring bits in a long series of lengthy interviews I did with Trump, a reality TV star at the time. “I never got it. It seemed so boring. But when I started building golf courses I did. Building a golf course is like gardening but on a much bigger scale.”

As a golf-course owner, Trump would often spar with different architects and contractors — some Fazio family members; Jack Nicklaus; various others — insisting he had superior ideas for the locations of cart paths, halfway houses, practice areas, elevated tees on man-made hills, excavated greenside ponds and waterfalls. He loved waterfalls.

There was some sort of exhale eight months ago by the people who orchestrate the biggest golf tournaments across the Atlantic Ocean. The kick-start of the war in Iran began on Feb. 28, just two weeks after the DP World Tour finished the last of four consecutive tournaments in the region.

The United Arab Emirates and its transit and economic hub of the Middle East, Dubai, was one of the areas attacked, roughly one month after many of the best golfers in the world competed in the Dubai Desert Classic. Due to a flight stoppage out of the country, LIV golfers struggled to travel to their next event in early March. Tommy Fleetwood, who lives in Dubai, was unable to see his family for over a month. Golf.copy:
- Super League plans faced fierce backlash from fans Back in the spring of 2021, it was revealed that 12 heavyweight outfits had agreed to form their own competition - with the plan being to welcome 20 teams into that pack. Premier League giants City, Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham were all involved. The so-called ‘Big Six’ faced serious backlash from supporters, with the proposals eventually being ripped up. The shadow of a Super League has, however, continued to loom large - with the likes of Real Madrid and Juventus refusing to scrap the plans entirely. Part of the problem for those considering a severing of ties with UEFA and FIFA is that any player on their books would no longer be eligible to represent their respective countries in international tournaments - which would make it difficult for transfers to be agreed. There would, however, be greater freedom when it comes to recruitment, with FFP and PSR regulations being removed. That would allow the likes of City, and other teams with super wealthy owners, to splash the cash as they see fit. Those at the Etihad Stadium are currently locked in an FFP battle that sees 114 charges hanging over the blue half of Manchester and the harshest of punishments being mooted. If City decided that they no longer wanted to dance to the Premier League’s tune, and that of the Football Association, could they be tempted to enter back into Super League construction discussions?

- Getty Why players would be against a European Super League When that question was put to Mills, the former City defender - who was speaking in association with Gambling.com, the guide to the best online casinos - told GOAL: “It's very, very difficult. “I've had this discussion many, many times. To play international football, FIFA have to ratify your competition. So if FIFA don't ratify your Super League, none of those players can play in international competition. “Now, as much as we think players favour club over country, when it comes to World Cups, European Championships, you win the Premier League, you win the Champions League, you're a legend at your football club, a legend in your city. You win the World Cup, you win the Euros, you're a legend of your country, you get knighthoods, it's there forever. “If I said to you now, who won the Champions League in 2017? You probably don't know without looking it up. There's a limit to the impact that has. But if I said name all those countries who won the World Cups, you can pretty much list them. You know who they are. “So I don't think the Super League will ever have legs in that way. Saudi have kind of tried it, it hasn't really worked. China tried it before, that didn't really work. You're always going to need competition. And the best players will still always want to play international football.”
