Golf.title: 'Tightest golf course I've ever played': Pros face suffocating test this week
Golf.summary: The field at this week’s DP World India Championship are battling a different kind of test in the Lodhi Course at Delhi Golf Club. The post ‘Tightest golf course I’ve ever played’: Pros face suffocating test this week appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Patrick Reed, Rory McIlroy, Thomas Detry and Tommy Fleetwood are among the players facing the Lodhi Course at Delhi Golf Club, host of this week's DP World India Championship. The course measures only 6,912 yards but has doglegs, pinched landing zones, thick rough and fairways lined by jungle and Mughal-era ruins. Detry swapped his driver for a 3-iron and shot a five-under 67 in the rain-shortened first round, one behind Niklas Norgaard. Only about half the field finished the round.

McIlroy also left his driver out of the bag, saying his best chance of winning lay in keeping it there. Fleetwood, who won the inaugural event last year at 22 under for his eighth DP World Tour title, shot a two-under 70 on Thursday. He said the rough is more penal this year and compared it to a U.S. Open. Reed said the narrow fairways mean a missed fairway is effectively a reload, and that the course feels like an irons-only test.
Golf.copy:
Patrick Reed has made 448 starts in his professional golf career, from California to Qatar to Kawagoe (that’s in Japan) — and everywhere in between. But even for the well-traveled Masters champ, this week’s stop is a new one.

“Never come around a golf course like this before,” he said Wednesday. “It’s one of those that it’s completely different than I would expect.” Reed was referencing the Lodhi Course at Delhi Golf Club, site of this week’s DP World India Championship. The course plays just 6,912 yards all stretched out, but is tighter than a 15-handicapper playing Augusta National with Tiger Woods. Doglegs. Pinched landing zones. Ball-gobbling rough. Fairways lined by jungle and Mughal-era ruins. You name it, DGC throws it at all comers.

bullets: Jon Rahm has reached a separation agreement with LIV Golf, which takes effect if Judge Michael B. Kaplan of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey approves it on 5 November. That included $7.5m from a single period and reportedly more than $100m in current and future payments.

Rahm regains the rights to his name, image and likeness, including his "Rahmbo" logo and the Legion XIII logo, though he cannot use the Legion XIII mark in another golf league such as TGL. He gives up any equity in the Legion XIII team and any further claim against LIV. LIV is in Chapter 11 after Saudi PIF withdrew funding, and its lawyers expect to know by the end of the month whether to press on with "LIV 2.0" for 2027 or wind down. Kaplan of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey on Nov. 5, Rahm will be free to play anywhere he can get a spot, while LIV will be free of its largest unsecured creditor.

The hundred-million-dollar question, then: what happens to the massive sums of money still owed to Rahm? LIV’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy filings revealed Rahm was owed $7.5 million just from a single period, a small percentage of what was reportedly more than $100 million in current and future payments left on his deal.

bullets: Anna La, a 21-year-old University of Georgia senior who did not grow up playing golf, spent last summer on a three-month social-media internship with Callaway in Carlsbad, California. She got it through the USGA's Pathways Launch, which has just completed its first year. The programme placed 24 participants in summer roles at 10 organisations, including the LPGA, PGA of America, PGA Tour, Dick's Sporting Goods/Golf Galaxy, Golf Pride, Pebble Beach Company and Pinehurst Resort & Country Club.

The paid internships are jointly funded by the USGA and the host organisations. They aim to widen golf's workforce pipeline to people from underrepresented backgrounds. Of the first cohort, one participant was hired full-time by their host organisation, another received a similar offer, and two found jobs through programme connections. The USGA said more than 90 per cent of participants were encouraged to pursue a golf career. Applications for the 2027 programme are open, and La has won the Golf Writers Association of America scholarship for 2026-27.
Golf.copy:
Twenty-one-year-old Anna La grew up in Georgia without meaningful exposure to golf. Today, the University of Georgia senior is plotting a career in the game. La has blazed her unlikely trail thanks in large part to a three-month social-media internship with Callaway last summer — an opportunity fostered by the USGA’s Pathways Launch, a program that offers 24 participants summer gigs at 10 organizations across the golf industry.

Pathways Launch, which just completed its first year, is designed for graduate and undergraduate students seeking to work in golf or sports. The paid internships are funded jointly by both the USGA and the participating organizations, which include the LPGA, PGA of America and PGA Tour, Dick’s Sporting Goods/Golf Galaxy, Golf Pride, Pebble Beach Company and Pinehurst Resort & Country Club. Each organization offers positions that emphasize the development of on-the-job skills, mentorship and leadership training.

Golf.title: 7 Unwritten Women’s Golf Rules That Need To Disappear

bullets: A Golf Monthly feature sets out seven unwritten rules at golf clubs that it argues hinder women who want to progress after trying the game. The piece also calls for club professionals to teach etiquette in lessons so golfers do not learn by trial and error, and for an end to midweek-only ladies' days and male-dominated Saturday morning tee times. It argues for mixed play and open competitions across weekdays and weekends, noting that England Golf's 2026 workshops identify time, accessibility and value for money as major barriers.
Golf.copy:
When I speak to female non-golfers, there is still a huge amount of obvious stigma attached to the game that stops them from giving it a go. The usual excuses come up: “It takes all day,” “I can’t play golf until I’m retired,” and “It’s too expensive.”

For me, those are just standard excuses from anyone who isn’t yet interested in taking up the game. The real issues start once someone has tried golf, fallen in love with it, and wants to progress.

Golf.title: Is This The Finest Course Close To Central London? I Think So
Golf.summary: This first-class course with impeccable pedigree is less than 10 miles from the Tower of London as the raven flies
Golf.copy:
Just a few miles from the heart of the capital, Royal Wimbledon Golf Club dates back to 1865 when play began over a seven-hole course. After a few years, this was expanded to a full 18 before the club was awarded its regal title in 1882. Many of its early members were influential in the evolution of The R&A, helped to inaugurate events such as the Amateur Championship and were involved in the creation of prestigious courses such as Royal St George's.

The club moved to Warren Farm and Caesar's Camp – an iron-age hill fort that skirts the 6th hole – in 1907, with Willie Park Junior masterminding the new layout. The great Harry Colt was a member, and he redesigned the course in 1924. Despite more recent changes to the 1st, 6th and 18th holes and some excellent bunker remodelling over the last few years by Tom Mackenzie, this is still fundamentally a Colt design and fully deserving of its place on the Golf Monthly Next 100 list.

bullets: Judge Michael B. Kaplan approved the restructuring support agreement between LIV Golf and BC Partners Global at Wednesday's Chapter 11 hearing. Rob Fitzgerald of Gibson Dunn, the attorney representing LIV, also said that the organisation would know by the end of the month if it could continue in a 'LIV 2.0' guise.

Golf.title: LIV golf: Organisation concerned by DP Tour's 'attempt to interfere' in player discussions
Golf.summary: LIV golf: Organisation concerned by DP Tour's 'attempt to interfere' in player discussions BBC
bullets: LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of a "clear attempt to interfere" with its restructuring after the European tour said it would refuse membership to anyone playing on LIV next season. LIV attorney Rob Fitzgerald of Gibson Dunn made the claim at a hearing in New Jersey Bankruptcy Court on Wednesday, and Judge Michael B. Kaplan said the comments raised concerns. Fitzgerald said LIV needs enough players signed up for a bona fide league by 25 October and expects a decision on LIV 2.0 by the end of the month.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 protection in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding, and hopes to conclude restructuring in early 2027. It owes its players at least $45m (£33m). On Wednesday, 19 player contracts, including those of Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson, were rejected. Rory McIlroy said the DP World Tour is within its rights to change its rules, and Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed said he had been accepted "from day one" after returning to the tour.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of a "clear attempt to interfere" with its restructuring process, after the European tour said it would refuse membership to anyone playing on the breakaway circuit next season.

During a court hearing on Wednesday, the attorney representing LIV said that the organisation was "quite concerned" by the stance taken by the rival DP World Tour. Rob Fitzgerald of Gibson Dunn, the attorney representing LIV, also said that the organisation would know by the end of the month if it could continue in a 'LIV 2.0' guise.

Golf.title: What's the optimal tee height for maximizing driving distance?
Golf.summary: What's the optimal tee height for maximizing your distance off the tee? Twenty years ago, GOLF Magazine ran an experiment to find out. The post What’s the optimal tee height for maximizing driving distance? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Golf instruction is ever-evolving, but the best advice stands the test of time. In GOLF.com’s series, Timeless Tips, we’re highlighting some of the greatest advice teachers and players have dispensed in the pages of GOLF Magazine. Today we look back at our June 2006 issue when we published the results of an experiment to find out the perfect tee height for maximizing distance with the driver.

Since advanced analytics have shed light on how important driving distance is for scoring, golfers of all abilities have been doing everything they can to add yards off the tee.

Golf.title: Patrick Reed: American reassures former LIV Golf colleagues - 'DP World Tour welcomed me in after I left breakaway league'
Golf.summary: Patrick Reed: American reassures former LIV Golf colleagues - 'DP World Tour welcomed me in after I left breakaway league' Sky Sports
bullets: Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed has said the DP World Tour welcomed him after he left LIV Golf, offering reassurance to former colleagues weighing their futures. New rules will require all members to state explicitly that they will not sign up for the proposed LIV 2.0 relaunch. Reed joined the DP World Tour after his LIV contract expired in January, and he leads Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy with four events remaining.

Reed said he felt the players had accepted him "from day one" and that he had played big, small and mid-level events alike. McIlroy, who is seeking a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, said he would vote for LIV deserters to be accepted. All three are in contention at this week's DP World India Championship, where McIlroy said he saw a good chance to cut into Reed's lead.
Golf.copy:
Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed offered some reassurance to former LIV Golf colleagues considering their futures by insisting he has been welcomed by the DP World Tour. New rules will require all members of the former European Tour to state explicitly that they will not be signing up for the proposed LIV 2.0 relaunch after the original format applied for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

The PGA Tour's year-long suspension policy means the DP World Tour has offered a safe haven, with Reed signing up after his contract expired in January. It has proved profitable as he is in contention to be only the second American to win the Race to Dubai as he leads Spaniard Eugenio Chacarra, himself a former LIV golfer, and Rory McIlroy with four events remaining.

Golf.title: Will Zalatoris to miss entire 2027 season with spinal-fusion surgery
Golf.summary: Will Zalatoris said he will undergo spiral-fusion surgery next month to correct ongoing back issues and will miss the entire 2027 season. The post Will Zalatoris to miss entire 2027 season with spinal-fusion surgery appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Will Zalatoris said on Wednesday, at media day for the Austin Championship, that he will have spinal-fusion surgery in Dallas next month to correct ongoing back problems. He will miss the entire 2027 PGA Tour season. The procedure is similar to the one Tiger Woods had, though with a different surgeon.

Zalatoris has finished second at both the Masters and the PGA Championship and has one PGA Tour win. He missed part of the 2026 season with a torn labrum, after recovering from back surgery in 2025. He said he hurt his back again at the Valero Texas Open in San Antonio this spring, trying to play 27 holes in cool weather, which was his last event of the year. After speaking with the Tour, he hopes to return in 2028 and play the Challenger Series.
Golf.copy:
AUSTIN — Will Zalatoris, who has battled injuries for much of his promising PGA Tour career, said Wednesday that he will undergoing spinal-fusion surgery in Dallas next month to correct ongoing back issues and will miss the entire 2027 PGA Tour season.

“I’ve been through four years of hell so it’s good to have something that will hopefully correct it,” Zalatoris said during media day for the Austin Championship. “It’s not something you want to do, but when you have three Tour physical therapists tell you it needs to be done at some time, you go ahead and do it.”

Golf.summary: I've always been a 'play whatever you can get' kind of guy, but when our new product finder recommended my optimal golf ball I had to give it a try...

Golf.title: 'They didn't give a s---’: Pro slams LIV players trying to make DP World Tour return
Golf.summary: Six-time winner Joost Luiten blasted LIV players hoping to rejoin the DP World Tour, and the tour itself, in a new interview. The post ‘They didn’t give a s—’: Pro slams LIV players trying to make DP World Tour return appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Joost Luiten, a 40-year-old six-time DP World Tour winner, told Today's Golfer that LIV Golf players seeking a DP World Tour return in 2027 "didn't give a s—" about the tour when they left for the money. The tour's 2027 decision lets former LIV players come back provided they have paid outstanding fines and do not sign with LIV 2.0, while LIV continues bankruptcy proceedings.

Luiten, ranked 67th in the Race to Dubai, argued that returning players take invitations from those who stayed loyal and from young talent. He said players who give up membership should lose their exemptions and suggested they go through Q School. Rory McIlroy backed the tour's right to change its rules at the DP World India Championship. The day before, at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, he said former LIV players should also be welcomed back to the PGA Tour.
Golf.copy:
The DP World Tour’s decision to ban LIV Golf pros from its tournaments in 2027 was a win for those who wish to see LIV end. And the European circuit stands to benefit from an influx of LIV stars as a result of that decision.

But not everyone on the DP World/PGA Tour side of golf’s civil war is happy with the outcome. Joost Luiten is one of those people. In a new interview with Today’s Golfer, the 40-year-old, six-time DP World Tour winner unloaded on LIV Golf pros hoping to return to the DP World Tour, and on the DP World Tour itself.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy's biggest weapon is in his hotel room this week

Delhi Golf Club measures 6,912 yards, with narrow fairways flanked by thick rough, dense jungle and ancient tomb ruins. Last season 42 per cent of the field played without a driver, according to Inside Tour Golf, and Tommy Fleetwood won with a mini driver as his longest club. Golf.copy:

But for the second straight year, this week’s DP World Tour host site, Delhi Golf Club, will take McIlroy’s biggest weapon out of his hands. In fact, McIlroy said Wednesday his driver may not even reach the grounds at the DP World India Championship.

bullets: Patrick Reed said he has felt welcomed back "since day one" on the DP World Tour after quitting LIV Golf in January, having missed traditional golf. Patrick Reed says he feels he has been welcomed back "since day one" after he quit LIV Golf at the turn of the year. Reed was among the first wave of players to be recruited by the breakaway tour in 2022 and was expected to extend his stay beyond this season.

But the American made the surprise decision to walk away from LIV in January because he missed the experience of traditional golf. Reed wasn't given the Brooks Koepka treatment and will return to the PGA Tour next season.

Golf.title: 'LIV is in such a state of flux': Rory McIlroy defends tour's new anti-LIV rule
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy mounted a defense of the DP World Tour's new LIV ban during his press conference ahead of the 2026 DP World India Championship. The post ‘LIV is in such a state of flux’: Rory McIlroy defends tour’s new anti-LIV rule appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy defended the DP World Tour's ban on LIV Golf players in 2027 at a press conference at Delhi Golf Club on Wednesday, two days after the announcement. He said tour leaders were 'well within their rights' to change rules to protect their business. Players who sign for LIV in 2027 cannot play DP World Tour events and will not be eligible for the European Ryder Cup team.

McIlroy said the DP World Tour is a members' organisation, as is the PGA Tour, and members agree to abide by its rules each year. He said the tour had been 'more than accommodating' to LIV players while it works on its strategic alliance with the PGA Tour and LIV is 'in such a state of flux'. Previously, players who paid fines could play most events and stay Ryder Cup eligible.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy is back in action this week at the 2026 DP World India Championship. There, he hopes to gain ground on Patrick Reed as he eyes his record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title.

A different topic, though, is hanging over the proceedings in India this week: the DP World Tour’s newly announced ban on LIV Golf players in 2027. On Wednesday morning, just two days after the tour announced its major LIV decision, McIlroy sat down for a press conference at Delhi Golf Club. Though his Race-to-Dubai chase did not come up while fielding reporters’ questions, the DP World Tour’s new anti-LIV rule did.

Golf.title: LIV Golf back in court for key hearing
Golf.summary: LIV Golf back in court for key hearing Sports Business Journal
bullets: LIV Golf has a Chapter 11 bankruptcy hearing in New Jersey on Wednesday, beginning at 1pm ET. It will seek court approval to terminate existing player contracts so it can proceed with LIV 2.0, including proposed player compensation and ownership structure. The plans include a 10-event schedule and purses second only to the PGA Tour globally.

Approval of LIV's restructuring support agreement with lead investor BC Partners would also let the league rehire employees and sign golf course agreements for 2027. The mid-October deadline to sign players has been extended to 25 October, and BC Partners can extend or waive it. The hearing follows news that the DP World Tour will no longer allow LIV players to be members, a major blow because European Ryder Cup hopefuls must be members. LIV says it remains on track with its player plans despite Jon Rahm's decision not to play LIV 2.0.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf has its latest Chapter 11 bankruptcy hearing later Wednesday in New Jersey, and with it comes a number of milestones for the league as it tries to launch LIV 2.0. In the hearing, which begins at 1pm ET, LIV will be seeking court approval to terminate existing contracts with players so that it can move forward with various plans as part of LIV 2.0. Among those include proposed compensation for players, as well as player ownership structure. LIV has plans for a 10-event schedule, and purse sizes that rank second only to the PGA Tour globally.

The league initially had a mid-October deadline to sign players for LIV 2.0, but that now has been extended to Oct. 25. And BC Partners, the league’s lead investor, has the right to extend or even waive that deadline. Even with Jon Rahm’s decision not to play LIV 2.0, the league has maintained that it is on track with its player plans for its next iteration.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy Is Right About The LIV Golf Failure
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy Is Right About The LIV Golf Failure Yahoo Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy told the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that LIV Golf "had probably half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly". He said the league could have used its money better than enriching tour pros who were already well paid. LIV filed for bankruptcy protection in September after cancelling its season finale in Michigan, though $300m from BC Partners offers some hope.

Unpaid prize money and appearance fees totalled more than $45m at the time of filing. Jon Rahm tops the unsecured creditors with a $7.5m claim, and Cameron Smith is fourth with more than $4.8m owed. Joost Luiten said returning players should face a harder route back, and the DP World Tour is introducing a rule to ban LIV 2.0 signees from the 2027 season.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf is collapsing because it lacked a smart plan for its massive wealth. The league filed for bankruptcy protection in September after canceling its season finale in Michigan. While some hope remains due to $300 million from BC Partners, the fundamental strategy failed to hold the golf world together.

Rory McIlroy believes the league's leadership missed the mark on how to use their funds. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, McIlroy said, "LIV had probably half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly." The PGA Tour loyalist noted that the league had plenty of money but wasted it. According to Fox Sports, McIlroy stated, "They certainly could have done better things with it instead of just enriching tour pros that were already making a lot of money."

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy has lost friends over LIV Golf – but the next big move is dividing his rivals
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy has lost friends over LIV Golf – but the next big move is dividing his rivals Today's Golfer
bullets: Rory McIlroy said he has drifted from some players who joined LIV Golf, particularly former European Ryder Cup team-mates. Speaking at a Bloomberg conference in New Delhi before the DP World India Championship, he said a difference of opinion over golf's future was not a reason to lose friends, but they stopped seeing each other once those players were ineligible for the Ryder Cup and the majors. He described LIV as a "half good idea poorly executed" and no longer a threat as it tries to relaunch and survive bankruptcy.

The next question is how returning players are reintegrated. The PGA Tour appears set on a one-year ban, while the DP World Tour must balance star names against its current members. Eddie Pepperell said the tour must handle the return of 15 to 20 LIV players across the season carefully. Joost Luiten said it should be made harder for them to return. McIlroy acknowledged loyal members might feel hard done by, but said he would vote for the players to return because it is good for business.
Golf.copy:
The avalanche of chaos that arrived with LIV Golf strained not only on professional relationships but also personal ones. Rory McIlroy, who said long ago he “hated” the LIV product as a staunch defender of the PGA Tour, admits he has drifted from a handful players who defected to the breakaway league.

The Masters champion most notably had a fallout with Sergio Garcia and at one stage was branded “immature” by the Spaniard. The pair seem to have reconciled, but there was also a war of words recently with Lee Westwood, who claimed McIlroy’s comments about the value of LIV players were “not thought out” and “typical Rory”.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy welcomes back LIV Golf rivals as exodus continues
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy welcomes back LIV Golf rivals as exodus continues bunkered.co.uk
bullets: Rory McIlroy said he would vote to let LIV Golf players return to the DP World Tour and PGA Tour, telling Bloomberg ahead of the DP World India Championship that "a rising tide lifts all boats". He said LIV had "half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly", with much of its capital wasted instead of being used to partner with governing bodies. LIV lost the support of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund earlier this year and filed for bankruptcy protection last month.

Players leaving LIV include its No.1 player Jon Rahm and fellow Spaniard David Puig, with Adrian Meronk, Abraham Ancer and Joaquin Niemann also reportedly following. Rahm will most likely have to spend a season on the DP World Tour before returning to the PGA Tour in 2028. McIlroy said he and Tiger Woods probably had the most to lose when LIV emerged in 2022, given their PGA Tour ties and the launch of TGL. He added that he has grown less close to some former European Ryder Cup team-mates.
Golf.copy:

Rory McIlroy has been a long-time critic of LIV Golf, but the six-time major champion is ready to welcome the league’s players back to the DP World Tour and PGA Tour.

Having lost the support of the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia (PIF) earlier this year, those at LIV – who filed for bankruptcy protection last month – are battling to keep the league alive.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy makes Tiger Woods admission with latest thoughts on LIV Golf
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy makes Tiger Woods admission with latest thoughts on LIV Golf Golfmagic
bullets: Rory McIlroy said he would support the return of players who defected to LIV Golf, telling Bloomberg in New Delhi that the league "had probably half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly". He said LIV's capital was partly wasted on enriching tour pros who were already well paid, when it could have partnered with governing bodies. LIV is fighting to survive Chapter 11 bankruptcy after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew. It has a $300m investment from BC Partners, and players have until 25 October to commit.

McIlroy said he and Tiger Woods "had the most to lose" when LIV launched in 2022, as they were about to start TGL, which required PGA Tour membership. He said some players who went to LIV were therefore lost to TGL. He also said he had grown apart from some former European Ryder Cup team-mates, not because of their differing views but because they no longer played the same events. The DP World Tour has said players who commit to LIV's 2027 season cannot keep their membership.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has admitted he rallied so hard against LIV Golf in the beginning because he and Tiger Woods had more to lose. The six-time major champion has now revealed he would support the return of players who defected to the Saudi-backed circuit, insisting the breakaway league no longer represents the same threat to professional golf as it did when it first launched in 2022.

McIlroy has been one of LIV Golf's most vocal opponents since its formation, but recent developments have raised further questions about the league's long-term future. LIV Golf is fighting for its future and, despite securing a $300m investment from BC Partners, continues to face uncertainty.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy's chasing his next big goal. In his way? Patrick Reed
Golf.summary: Two years ago this Rory McIlroy-Patrick Reed showdown would have seemed impossible. This week in India is a reminder of what's changed. The post Rory McIlroy’s chasing his next big goal. In his way? Patrick Reed appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed are both in New Delhi for the DP World India Championship, each chasing Race to Dubai points. Reed leads the standings, with Eugenio Chacarra second and McIlroy third. McIlroy has won the title seven times, including four years in a row, and an eighth would equal Colin Montgomerie's record.

Reed left LIV Golf and was suspended from the PGA Tour, which left him free to play the DP World Tour, where he began winning. His suspension is now over and he will earn one of the tour's 10 cards for 2027. Finishing ahead of every other non-PGA Tour member would also earn him a place in the Signature events. The pair's rivalry dates to the 2016 Ryder Cup, and the playoffs in Abu Dhabi and Dubai follow in a month.
Golf.copy:
They’re meeting on a new battleground. And with something decidedly different at stake. We’re now a decade into the McIlroy-Reed rivalry. The two tangled in singles at the 2016 Ryder Cup and in the final group at Augusta National in the 2018 Masters. They chose opposite sides in the LIV Golf-PGA Tour saga. Reed’s lawyer subpoenaed McIlroy on Christmas Eve in 2022. Things got chippy on the driving range in Dubai in 2023. You get the idea; these two won’t soon be going on holiday together.

But they have ended up in New Delhi together this week, each chasing valuable points as the finish line gets closer in the DP World Tour’s Race to Dubai. It’s a title McIlroy has won four years in a row and seven times overall, which has him just one shy of Colin Montgomerie’s record, which he dearly covets. He’s currently third in the rankings. Reed holds the lead.

Golf.title: Their golf course is becoming a data center. But first, an emotional farewell
Golf.summary: On Monday, golfers bid farewell to Dauphin Highlands, a popular Pennsylvania golf course now owned by a data-center developer. The post Their golf course is becoming a data center. But first, an emotional farewell appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Dauphin Highlands, a public golf course near Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, closed on Monday, with more than 300 golfers playing a final round. The Dauphin County General Authority sold the 228-acre site to a Texas-based developer for $45m to make way for a 400,000-square-foot, $10bn data centre. The authority says the course was losing money and had accrued $13m in debt.

Local officials say the deal will bring tens of millions of dollars in community benefits, including public safety and municipal infrastructure improvements. Construction is not due to start until next year, although test drilling has begun. The course opened on Labor Day weekend in 1995 on land that was previously a Bethlehem Steel retreat, and director of instruction Tim Birney, 77, has worked there since 2012.
Golf.copy:
Dauphin Highlands, a popular public golf course near Harrisburg, Pa., opened on Labor Day weekend in 1995. Tim Birney, now 77, was on the tee sheet that day. He still remembers being taken by the natural beauty of the Bill Love design, which sits on a pastoral 228-acre plot overlooking the Susquehanna River.

“It looked like it’d been there forever,” Birney told me. Monday was Dauphin Highlands’ last day of operation, as the golf course prepares to make way for construction of a 400,000-square-foot, $10 billion data center. Many residents, especially golfers, were holding out hope that the day would never come, but it did — the result of the Dauphin County General Authority’s decision to sell the parcel to Texas-based data-center developer for $45 million.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy's newest sponsorship includes an insane travel perk
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy's newest sponsor is sprinkling in a mind-blowing, first-of-its-kind travel perk for the grand slam winner. The post Rory McIlroy’s newest sponsorship includes an insane travel perk appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy has added DP World as a new partner, with the Dubai-based logistics company to help with his travel logistics through the season. DP World will also set up two personalised fitness and recovery trailers at every tournament he plays, wherever in the world it is held. The announcement came ahead of this week's DP World India Championship, where McIlroy is playing for the second straight year.

The trailers will contain strength and cardio equipment, a cold plunge, an infrared sauna and a Hyperice recovery station. DP World already holds the naming rights to the European Tour and the India Championship. McIlroy said in a sponsored social media post that having the same environment to train and recover in every week gives him and his team one less thing to think about, adding that consistency matters when competing around the world.
Golf.copy:
Most of life as a professional golfer is glamorous. Travel is not. For those lucky enough to ply their trade in golf, life on the road includes some version of the same experience every week: hotels, rental homes, airports, rental car lines, lost bags, and enough credit card points to fill an ocean liner. And among that group, travel is viewed one way: as a necessary evil, a thing that comes with the pursuit of a lifelong dream.

Hell, even for those in pro golf with the means to pay for every travel luxury, the goal isn’t enjoyment of life on the road. It’s to eliminate friction, to take the hardships of the “road” out of “life on the road” — an annoyance rendered moot by private planes and private chefs and private homes and personal assistants.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: My ball won't stop rolling when I place it. What now?
Golf.summary: What do you do if your ball won't stop rolling when you place it? How should you proceed? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: My ball won’t stop rolling when I place it. What now? appeared first on Golf .
bullets: In this Rules Guy column, a reader asks about a ball resting on the lip of a bunker, held in place by a rake handle. When the rake is moved and the ball replaced, it rolls closer to the hole into a better lie in the fairway. The answer is that the player cannot play from the new position. The rake is a movable obstruction, and under Rule 15.2 the ball must be put back.

If the ball will not stay put after a second attempt, Rule 14.2e says the player must find the nearest spot in the correct area, not nearer the hole, where it will stay. A second reader asks about a ball on a green that was blown off by a gust of wind during a ruling delay for a playing partner. Under Rule 9.3, a ball moved by natural forces is played as it lies, unless it had already been lifted and replaced.
Golf.copy:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. My approach shot landed on the lip of the bunker, held in place by the handle of the sand rake. If I move the handle, the ball drops into the sand trap. The rules state the rake is a movable object and can be moved with the ball replaced to its original spot. Here’s the rub: the ball won’t stay put — it rolls down the shoulder of the bunker closer to the hole, and in a more favorable lie in the fairway. Can I play from the new position? —Richard Fetterman, Banning, CA

Nice and reasonable though that may sound, Richard, verily you cannot. Though it was held in place by the rake, your ball came to rest on a specific spot. That rake, as you note, is a movable obstruction, but per Rule 15.2 you need to put the ball back if it then moves.

bullets: A golf instructor describes a lesson with a former mini-tour player, Travis, who had developed early extension. He stood up out of his posture, stopped rotating and flipped the club through impact. The fix started earlier in the swing, with the clubface on the takeaway and then his trail arm, which he over-bent on the backswing, flattening the top of his swing and creating a steep transition.

To build structure in the trail arm, Travis used the AMG Arm Shark, a strap with a magnetic fin that releases with a noise when the arm moves outside the correct range. He then hit balls at three-quarter speed at most to ingrain the pattern. An alignment stick gave feedback on hip depth, and maintaining that depth improved his path and strike, so he stopped catching the ball toward the toe.
Golf.copy:
A recent lesson with my friend Travis reinforced something that’s important to remember no matter where you’re getting your golf instruction: If you want to fix something in your swing, you have to fix the cause. Too many golfers just chase symptoms.

Travis is a former mini-tour player who’s taught the game himself, so he’s no stranger to instruction. But early extension had crept into his swing anyway, just as it does for players who’ve never even been on a lesson tee. Coming down, he’d stand up out of his posture, stop rotating and flip the club through impact, trying to launch the ball higher and add speed.

bullets: Writing as a low single-figure handicapper, the author argues that autumn offers the best conditions for low scoring after a dry UK summer left courses firm and fast. Dew tracks on the greens aid green reading, less bright sunlight makes the ball easier to see, and cooler temperatures reduce heat exhaustion. A medical friend told the author that a calmer circadian rhythm in autumn encourages a slower pace and a more fluid swing.

Golf.title: ‘You did your absolute worst’: Work on Trump's D.C. muni enrages judge
Golf.summary: A ‘furious’ judge on Monday lit into the Trump administration for removing more than 400 trees from East ​Potomac Golf Links. The post ‘You did your absolute worst’: Work on Trump’s D.C. muni enrages judge appeared first on Golf .
bullets: A judge on Monday criticised the Trump administration after 430 trees were removed from East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C., despite her order requiring advance notice of substantive work, including felling 10 or more trees. The government filed notice at 4:55pm on Friday, hours before the work began, and says about another 100 trees are to come down. Judge Reyes imposed a 24-hour halt on further removal, which could be extended to 14 days.

Reyes ordered Frank Lands, the National Park Service's deputy director for operations, to join the four-hour hearing. He said Interior deputy chief of staff Greg Wischer told him to proceed, and Wischer is expected to testify on Tuesday. The government says the removal follows a 2019 Cultural Landscape Report, which the plaintiffs, the DC Preservation League and two residents, dispute. The Interior took control of the course after terminating the National Links Trust's lease in December.
Golf.copy:
A ‘furious’ judge on Monday lit into the Trump administration for removing more than 400 trees from East Potomac Golf Links, the historic Washington, D.C., muni of which the Department of Interior controversially took control late last year.

The judge’s ire stemmed from a previous court order by which she had instructed the Interior Department to provide advance notice of substantive construction work on the property, including any plans to fell 10 or more trees.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan pulls back curtain on Titleist's secret prototype 3-wood
Golf.summary: After his win at the Baycurrent Classic, Michael Brennan gave some details of the prototype Titleist GTS fairway wood he's been using. The post Michael Brennan pulls back curtain on Titleist’s secret prototype 3-wood appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic in Japan on Sunday, his third career win and second in his last five starts. He led the field in driving accuracy, missing just five fairways all week, and gained over seven shots off the tee. With Yokohama Country Club measuring 7,322 yards, he often hit his Titleist GTS 3W Prototype fairway wood off the tee.

Brennan said he switched to the 3-wood at Colonial and finds its spin more consistent, with a slight right-bias miss that lets him swing hard. The prototype has a silver face and a single central sole weight, unlike the GTS2 and GTS3, which have flippable heel and toe weights. Titleist has released no details, and the article suggests the club may not reach retail until its next product cycle.
Golf.copy:
After picking up his third career win — and second in the last five starts — Michael Brennan is sharing some details on one of Titleist’s hottest prototype clubs. Brennan took home the Baycurrent Classic Sunday in Japan behind an outstanding display off the tee where he led the field in accuracy — missing just five fairways all week, including none on Sunday — while ranking eighth in driving distance. As you can imagine, Brennan naturally led in the field in SG: Off-the-Tee, picking up over seven shots, his best performance of the season.

Because Brennan is one of the longest hitters on the PGA Tour and Yokohama Country Club measures a modest (for the PGA Tour) 7,322 yards on the scorecard, Brennan certainly didn’t have to pull the big stick on every hole.

Golf.title: Your golf shoes are costing you speed. Here's what you should know
Golf.summary: Johnny Wunder visited the FootJoy Lab at the Titleist Performance Center and learned why finding the right shoe is more important than you think. The post Your golf shoes are costing you speed. Here’s what you should know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
When was the last time you actually thought about your golf shoes as a piece of performance equipment? If you’re like most guys — and frankly, if you were like me before walking into the FootJoy lab on Manchester Lane — you treat golf shoes like a fashion accessory OR just a plain comfort play. I’m that guy, and I knew nothing.

You walk into the shop, online or at a PGA TOUR Superstore, grab whatever size you’ve worn since you became an adult (because obviously I’m a size 10) and match them to whatever polo you’re rocking that day. Technology? Torsional stiffness? Total blind spot. In this realm, I’ll happily admit I was a complete idiot. My cohort Jake is way more versed in this world than I am. Like my Golf Pride fitting in Pinehurst, this was an eye opener.

Golf.title: Are Your Iron Shafts Too Heavy? The Small Gear Change That Saved This 8 -Handicapper's Game
Golf.summary: In my experience, up to 70% of golfers play iron shafts that are too heavy - here is how one simple gear change completely transformed a hapless 8-handicapper's game...
Golf.copy:
Over my years as a PGA Professional, I’ve custom-fit thousands of golfers, seeing virtually every swing type and equipment mismatch imaginable. But every now and then, a single tweak yields results so transformative it genuinely stops you in your tracks.

That exact scenario played out recently with my good friend and Kick Point podcast co-host, Dan Parker... Dan is a fairly typical 8-handicap player with a pretty solid all-round game, but having played together on numerous occasions, I had long felt that the 120-gram steel shafts in his Ping i230 irons were just far too heavy for him. On the course, he always seemed to be struggling to catch his arms and clubhead up to his body turn through impact. The inevitable result was a frustratingly inconsistent strike and dangerously unpredictable start directions.

Golf.title: LIV Golf 2.0: Who’s in and who’s out ahead of deadline day?
Golf.summary: LIV Golf 2.0: Who’s in and who’s out ahead of deadline day? Today's Golfer
bullets: LIV Golf players have until 25 October to decide whether to commit to the league's 2.0 relaunch, which is backed by a possible $300 million investment from credit firm BC Partners. Richard Bland is the first to commit, while Harry Tringale and Victor Perez have indicated they will stay. Jon Rahm's exit was confirmed through a New Jersey bankruptcy hearing, where his lawyer called the contract conditions "unacceptable".

Adrian Meronk and David Puig do not intend to play on LIV next season, and Sergio Garcia has exited his original contract and appears set to refuse the new terms. The relaunch is thought to hinge on Bryson DeChambeau, who has not declared his plans, and Joaquin Niemann is still weighing equity in LIV 2.0 against a possible DP World Tour schedule. The DP World Tour's decision to reject memberships for players joining LIV 2.0 has made the league's task harder.
Golf.copy:
Which players are leaving LIV Golf? And who is sticking around for the league’s 2.0 era? This is everything you need to know… The deadline for LIV Golf players to decide whether they will stick or twist is almost here.

The league has until October 25 to convince key names to sign up for the new iteration of the league ahead of a possible $300 million investment from credit firm BC Partners. And it is crucial that the league persuades some big hitters to stay for its relaunch. But the DP World Tour’s move to reject memberships for players who hope to sign up to LIV 2.0 has made LIV’s prospects a whole lot more difficult.

Golf.title: DP World Tour bans LIV Golf players for 2027, ending their Ryder Cup eligibility
Golf.summary: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings told BBC Sport that players who participate in LIV Golf 2.0 won't be allowed to play on the European circuit. The post DP World Tour bans LIV Golf players for 2027, ending their Ryder Cup eligibility appeared first on Golf .
bullets: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings told BBC Sport that the European circuit will no longer grant conditional releases to LIV players in 2027, saying "players need to make a choice". The earlier agreements, which let players such as Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton keep their Ryder Cup eligibility, applied only to the 2026 season. Players will now be asked to disclose which tours they intend to play, and any who sign a deal and then play LIV would have their membership terminated.

The deadline to apply for DP World Tour membership is 16 November, while players must commit to LIV Golf 2.0 by 25 October. LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew funding, and BC Partners has since agreed to back the relaunch as part of a targeted $300 million in cumulative financing, subject to court approval. The ban comes as the DP World Tour renegotiates its alliance with the PGA Tour, and the next hearing in LIV's bankruptcy case is on Wednesday 14 October.
Golf.copy:
Whatever becomes of LIV Golf 2.0, the DP World Tour has decided it won’t let those who compete in the rebel circuit’s new version have it both ways. In a statement to BBC Sport, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings said the European circuit, which had previously reached agreements with LIV players to allow them into its tournaments, will no longer do so in 2027, effectively banning them from playing.

“Players need to make a choice,” Kinnings told BBC Sport. “We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour.”

Golf.title: 'Bryson Playing A Full DP World Tour Schedule Would Be Electric'
Golf.summary: In this edition of Inside The Ropes, our editor and news team writers discuss the futures of LIV Golf, Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm...
bullets: Golf Monthly's team discusses the futures of LIV Golf, Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau as LIV's bankruptcy case continues and players decide whether to commit to the league or go elsewhere. Rahm, David Puig and Adrian Meronk have already left, and the DP World Tour has said it will not allow LIV players to be members in 2027.

The writers largely see LIV's future as uncertain rather than finished, noting it has lost Rahm and its Asian Tour feeder system and could lose Tyrrell Hatton and others, along with its OWGR points and Major pathways. They say DeChambeau committing his future could help the league, and that more than 40 other golfers outside the DP World Tour group might sign on. One writer argues the PGA Tour should allow Rahm straight back in, given his pull with viewers and ticket buyers.
Golf.copy:
'Inside The Ropes' is the chance for Golf Monthly's expert team to share its honest thoughts on the biggest subjects in the game. This time, it's all about the futures of Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and LIV Golf'.

It's set to be a critical next few weeks for LIV Golf and its hopes of a '2.0' version coming to fruition, with its bankruptcy case rolling on and players deciding whether to commit or go elsewhere.

Golf.title: Can A 3-Handicap Golfer Break Par If Rory McIlroy Hits The Tee Shots?
Golf.summary: What would you shoot if you played your second shot from a typical Rory McIlroy drive? Joel Tadman went to a ‘normal’ parkland course to find out
Golf.copy:
As a 3-handicap golfer, I'm relatively competent in all areas of the game but playing with the likes of colleague Sam De'Ath, who has a handicap of +4, I realise the gulf in skill between myself and an elite player. Then there's the next chasm in technique from elite level amateur to PGA Tour player, making my golfing ability feel especially ordinary relatively speaking.

Driving has always been one of my weaker areas too. But what if I could swap out my shambolic tee shots and sub in one of the best drivers of our generation? How would my short game hold up and could I shoot under par around a ‘normal’ parkland course?

Golf.copy:
Former European Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley says the DP World Tour has "a right to compete for business" after the circuit confirmed players intending to compete on LIV Golf in 2027 will not be eligible for membership.

DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings told BBC Sport that players must "make a choice" over where they play next season, with the circuit adopting a significantly tougher stance towards those seeking to compete on both tours.

Golf.title: 'I'm dejected': Late bogeys cost promising pro PGA Tour card
Golf.summary: Cole Hammer had one hand on a 2027 PGA Tour card before a poor final round at the Korn Ferry Tour Championship left him "dejected." The post ‘I’m dejected’: Late bogeys cost promising pro PGA Tour card appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Cole Hammer, 27, missed out on a PGA Tour card at the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour Championship after a final-round 73 left him tied 43rd. He began the week 20th in the season-long standings, the last position that earns a card, but five Sunday bogeys, including one on his second-to-last hole, dropped him to 22nd. David Lamb, who started the week 23rd, finished 20th to take the final card.

Hammer, who helped Texas win the 2022 NCAA title and was named the world's best amateur in 2019, said ball striking let him down and that he was "dejected". He added that he still believes in himself and described his pursuit of a card as "a fun journey" of five or six years of learning. He will play another season on the Korn Ferry Tour.
Golf.copy:
Sunday saw a host of young and journeyman pros alike experience the highlight of their careers: earning PGA Tour cards at the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour Championship. As happens every year, heartwarming tales about players’ big achievements abound. But there is another side to the story: the other pros who just missed out on their Tour cards.

On Sunday, the pain that group felt was best exemplified by Cole Hammer. The 27-year-old Texas pro narrowly lost his grasp on his own Tour card with a poor final round on Sunday. But instead of fleeing the course as fast as he could, a “dejected” Hammer faced the cameras and opened up about his unfortunate fate. In the process, he showed a hard-earned perspective that should serve him well as he continues his pro career.

Golf.title: I’ve Played Golf For 40 Years – These Are The 5 Biggest Lessons I've Learned
Golf.summary: I've played golf as a junior, a youth, a (just about) adult and a senior in waiting… It’s taught me quite a lot!
Golf.copy:
I’m lucky. I play golf. It’s one of the most giving, rewarding and facilitating activities that human beings in today's world can participate in. My entire life has been shaped by golf.

In my early days as a junior, great role models helped me enjoy the sport and taught me how to behave, not only within our hallowed game but also as part of the wider community and the wider world.

Golf.title: Jon Rahm reveals first start since LIV Golf exit
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm reveals first start since LIV Golf exit Today's Golfer
bullets: Jon Rahm will play the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month, his first start since his lawyer told LIV's bankruptcy court that he would not take part in LIV 2.0. It will be his first appearance at the DP World Tour Playoffs event, to be held at Yas Links. Rahm said he was looking forward to playing in Abu Dhabi before heading to Dubai the following week.

Under a deal agreed with the DP World Tour earlier this season, Rahm must play additional events to avoid punishment for clashing with LIV fixtures. He is 46th in the Race to Dubai rankings, and the top 50 reach the $10 million season-ending Tour Championship at Jumeirah Estates. He missed last week's Open de Espana because he and his wife Kelley are expecting a fourth child.
Golf.copy:
Jon Rahm has announced his first start since declaring he has quit LIV Golf. Last week, it was revealed in LIV’s bankruptcy courts that Rahm would not be signing up to the post-Saudi version of the breakaway league.

“Mr. Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0… and has determined that those terms are unacceptable to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0,” said the Spaniard’s attorney, John Beck.

We head to Delhi Golf Club, for the DP World India Championship 2026, which is sure to test the players in a way that few other tracks can. Golf.title: LIV Golf players to be banned from DP World Tour and Ryder Cup
Golf.summary: LIV Golf players to be banned from DP World Tour and Ryder Cup City AM
bullets: Players who sign up to a relaunched LIV Golf will be banned from the DP World Tour and so effectively from the Ryder Cup, according to the tour's chief Guy Kinnings. LIV has secured BC Partners funding to exit bankruptcy after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing. Players including Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Cameron Smith have been offered equity in the new business and have until 25 October to commit, though Rahm's lawyer has said he will not take part.

Joaquin Niemann, who has earned £60m in LIV prize money, does not hold DP World Tour status and would need to go through qualifying school or find a way onto the PGA Tour. LIV has sought court authority to terminate existing player agreements, a point due to be addressed at a wider hearing on Wednesday. CEO Scott O'Neil told the Sportico Invest London conference that the Trump organisation has been "tremendously supportive" of LIV.
Golf.copy:
Players who sign up to play on a resurrected LIV Golf tour will be prohibited from competing on the DP World Tour or in the Ryder Cup, its European chiefs have said. The rebel golf league has secured funding from BC Partners to exit bankruptcy proceedings after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund pulled its backing earlier this year.

Players including Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Cameron Smith have been offered equity in the new business and given until 25 October to pledge their continued allegiance. Rahm’s lawyer said he will not partake in the new season.

Golf.title: 'Players Need To Make A Choice'
Golf.summary: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings has outlined his circuit's much tougher policy in relation to LIV golfers from the start of next season
bullets: The DP World Tour will not allow any golfer involved in the new version of the LIV Golf League to hold membership from 2027, Golf Monthly understands, in a report first carried by BBC Sport. CEO Guy Kinnings said "players must make a choice" and that those unwilling to comply with the tour's rules should not seek to join it. The stance follows the Saudi PIF's April announcement that it would withdraw financial support for LIV, and eight conditional releases granted in February.

Roughly 15 players with status on both tours are likely to be affected, including Tyrrell Hatton, Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin. Only DP World Tour members will be eligible for Europe's Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor next year. Jon Rahm has ruled himself out of the new LIV league, so he looks set to return to the DP World Tour full-time in 2027. Joaquin Niemann and Thomas Pieters would have to enter Q-School or agree a deal for guaranteed invites, and a player who says they will not play LIV but then does so could have their membership cancelled immediately.
Golf.copy:
The DP World Tour will not allow any golfer involved in the new version of the LIV Golf League to obtain membership on the European circuit from 2027, Golf Monthly understands.

First reported by BBC Sport, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings is on record as saying "players must make a choice" in terms of where they will play next season and beyond. As it stands, it is possible for many LIV golfers to hold a DP World Tour card as well and compete without fines or sanctions after the Wentworth-based circuit granted eight conditional releases back in February.

Golf.title: DP World Tour to refuse LIV players in 2027 season
Golf.summary: The DP World Tour will not allow LIV Golf players to compete at its events in the 2027 season.
bullets: Players who sign up to LIV Golf next season will not be allowed to be DP World Tour members in 2027, in a significantly tougher stance than in recent seasons. Chief executive Guy Kinnings told BBC Sport that players "need to make a choice". About 15 LIV players, including Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin, hold status with the tour, and only members can play for Europe in the Ryder Cup.

Players will be asked to disclose which tours they intend to play, and failing to declare an intention to play LIV would be grounds for termination of membership. The change is understood to stem mainly from LIV offering players equity, seen as incompatible with a members organisation, and comes as the tour's alliance with the PGA Tour is negotiated. Players have until 16 November to sign up to the DP World Tour, while LIV must sign players by 25 October under its court-supervised restructuring.
Golf.copy:
Players who sign up to LIV Golf next season will not be allowed to be members of the European tour in 2027. The European tour, which is sponsored by DP World, said players must "make a choice" regarding where they play - a significantly tougher stance than in recent seasons.

Only players who are members of the DP World Tour can play for Europe in the Ryder Cup. Deadlines for both tours are in the next five weeks, though there remains uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf's future despite it securing a possible $300m in funding as it attempts to restructure.

Golf.title: Tour Confidential: Can LIV Golf survive without Jon Rahm?
Golf.summary: This week's Tour Confidential breaks down Jon Rahm's departure from LIV Golf's future. What does it mean for his PGA Tour prospects? The post Tour Confidential: Can LIV Golf survive without Jon Rahm? appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Jon Rahm is officially out of LIV Golf 2.0, his lawyer announced last week, a blow to a league that has recently filed for bankruptcy and already has few stars. Golf.com's writers said LIV could continue in a trimmed-down form, but Zephyr Melton argued it would no longer be a major player in global golf. Sergio Garcia and David Puig also appear to be out.

Attention now turns to Joaquin Niemann, Tyrrell Hatton and Bryson DeChambeau, whose decision is seen as the most significant. Rahm did not accept the Returning Member Program deal offered to Brooks Koepka, and PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp has said the programme had an expiry date. Josh Berhow suggested a one-year suspension as a minimum, while Sean Zak and Melton said Rahm should receive no exemption and should use the DP World Tour pathway.
Golf.copy:
Check in every week for the unfiltered opinions of our writers and editors as they break down the hottest topics in the sport, and join the conversation by tweeting us at @golf_com. This week, we discuss Jon Rahm’s decision to decline LIV 2.0 and what the PGA Tour should do about it.

Jon Rahm is officially out of LIV Golf 2.0, his lawyer announced last week, a major blow to the league that’s already treading water after recently filing for bankruptcy. With already few stars, can LIV Golf survive without Rahm on board?

Golf.title: Meet the 20 pros who just earned 2027 PGA Tour cards
Golf.summary: Twenty pros grabbed 2027 PGA Tour cards via their finish during the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour season. Here's who earned a promotion. The post Meet the 20 pros who just earned 2027 PGA Tour cards appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Twenty players, including 19-year-old Blades Brown, earned 2027 PGA Tour cards through the season-ending Korn Ferry Tour Championship on Sunday. The season-long points race was won by a former PGA Tour University graduate who won twice in 2026 and had six top-five finishes. Hitt won the Championship itself, in his third consecutive Korn Ferry season.

The cards give the group a head start before the Tour's two-track system debuts in 2028, when players will compete for a place in the top-tier Championship Series. Alistair Docherty, 32, advanced after four years on the Korn Ferry Tour. Morrison, who is 6ft 9in, earned his card in 131 days, and Johnson made 21 of 25 cuts in his eighth season. Lamb won the Club Car Championship earlier this year, which secured the last of the 20 cards.
Golf.copy:
If you haven’t heard, big changes are coming to the PGA Tour in 2028. With the Tour’s two-track system debuting in a little over a year, that means next season, 2027, will be critical for players trying to play their way onto the top tier, the Championship Series.

And you know what’s really going to help accomplish that? By already owning a PGA Tour card in 2027. Twenty players just did that — including a 19-year-old pro — as they earned a promotion via the season-ending Korn Ferry Tour Championship Sunday. Now those guys have a head start in getting on the top track come 2028.

Golf.title: Teenage phenom earns Tour card, sets record the hard way
Golf.summary: You've likely heard his name before, but you're about to see a lot more of this 19-year-old on the PGA Tour next season. The post Teenage phenom earns Tour card, sets record the hard way appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Blades Brown, 19, finished second in Sunday's final Korn Ferry Tour event, having squandered a fourth 54-hole lead. He still earned a full PGA Tour season for 2027 and became the youngest player to win a Tour card by graduating from the Korn Ferry Tour. He turned pro at 17 and has made 16 of 18 cuts this season, with five top-10 finishes.

Brown finished ninth in the season-long Korn Ferry race, which puts him near the alternate border for some early west coast events such as the Phoenix Open. Alongside his 18 Korn Ferry starts in 2026, he made 11 PGA Tour starts, making nine cuts and finishing in the top 20 seven times. He earned Special Temporary Membership but chose to pursue the feeder-tour route. He will remain a teenager until next year's PGA Championship.
Golf.copy:
Sunday may not have been the exact result 19-year-old Blades Brown was looking for — a fourth 54-hole lead squandered — but it ultimately saw him earn what he wanted next: a season full of starts on the PGA Tour.

Brown is well known to this point, partly due to his golfy name and partly due to his impressive game. He turned pro at just 17 and has played on the Korn Ferry Tour much of the last two seasons, occasionally sprinkling in some starts on the PGA Tour. He flashed in moments this summer, never quite getting across the line for a win, but the floor has been extremely high. He’s made 16 of 18 cuts and finished in the top 10 five times.

Golf.title: Which 20 Korn Ferry Tour Players Secured 2027 PGA Tour Cards?
Golf.summary: Following on from the Korn Ferry Tour Championship, a total of 20 players from the circuit have wrapped up their playing privileges on the PGA Tour for 2027
bullets: The PGA Tour has 20 new members for 2027 following the Korn Ferry Tour Championship at The Federal Club. Ross Steelman topped the final points list, with Sandy Scott, who won his last two starts, second. Austin Hitt won the finale by two shots and moved from outside the top 20 into sixth, while Alvaro Ortiz, younger brother of LIV's Carlos, finished fifth.

Nineteen-year-old Blades Brown, who had 12 top-25 finishes, placed in the top 10 and became the youngest player to earn a PGA Tour card via the Korn Ferry Tour. Carson Young and Taylor Dickson, who lost their cards in 2025, regained them. Davis Lamb rose three places to take the 20th and final card, helped by a solo eighth-place finish at the Championship.
Golf.copy:
After a lengthy 2026 season, where players battled it to further their careers, the PGA Tour now has 20 new members for 2027. Offering more prize money and opportunities to earn Major starts, the jump between the Korn Ferry Tour and PGA Tour is a sizeable one, hence why many will be relieved to secure their playing privileges on the latter for next year.

Prior to the Korn Ferry Tour Championship finale, which took place at The Federal Club, multiple names were already Tour bound and, following the conclusion of the event, we now know who is among the full list of players that find themselves inside the top 20.

Golf.title: Report: PGA Tour Caddie Resigns Mid-Tournament At Baycurrent Classic
Golf.summary: First reported by Golfweek, David Lipsky and his caddie, Darren Woolard, reportedly parted ways prior to the final round of the Baycurrent Classic on Sunday
bullets: David Lipsky's caddie, Darren Woolard, reportedly told him to find someone else to carry his bag before the final round of the Baycurrent Classic in Japan, according to Golfweek. Lipsky, 38, finished in a share of 54th at Yokohama Country Club on three under and shot a one-under 70 on Sunday. It is unclear who caddied for him, though some claim it was his trainer.

The event was won by Michael Brennan by one stroke over Keith Mitchell and Jacob Bridgeman. The split came a month after Alejandro Tosti's caddie, Cliff Ellis, walked off midway through the first round of the Biltmore Championship in September. Lipsky has made 160 PGA Tour starts and earned $8 million in prize money.
Golf.copy:
Players splitting with caddies is nothing new in the professional game but, in the last month, we have seen two players split with their loopers mid-event. The first came back at the Biltmore Championship in September, when Alejandro Tosti's caddie, Cliff Ellis, walked off midway through the first round, with the other occurring at this week's Baycurrent Classic.

Taking place in Japan, the 72-man tournament was won by Michael Brennan, who secured a one stroke win over Keith Mitchell and Jacob Bridgeman. Less than 12 hours on from the win, though, news broke that one player in the tournament had split with his caddie prior to a ball being struck on the final round on Sunday.

Golf.title: Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win
Golf.summary: Scotland's Grant Forrest holds off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year.
bullets: Scotland's Grant Forrest held off home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open, earning a place at The Open and the Masters next year. Chacarra was in the clubhouse on 13 under, so Forrest and Victor Perez needed birdies at the 18th. After Perez's putt drifted past, Forrest holed his to claim a third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

Forrest began the final round sharing the lead with England's Joe Dean on 13 under. He made bogeys at the third, sixth and eighth but recovered with three birdies and a bogey in five holes at the start of the back nine. A closing one-under 70 earned the £480,000 first prize. Forrest said he was in pure shock after a tough year and could not believe he was going to Augusta.
Golf.copy:
Scotland's Grant Forrest held off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year. With Chacarra in the clubhouse at 13 under, Forrest and playing partner Victor Perez needed to make birdies at the 18th to go above the Spaniard.

Both players' drives nestled down in the greenside rough on the 322-yard par four, and after Perez's birdie putt drifted past the hole, Forrest sunk his to seal his third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

Golf.title: How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson
Golf.summary: Alistair Docherty joined GOLF's Subpar podcast to discuss finally earning his PGA Tour card, his first golf memory and more. The post How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Alistair Docherty, 32, who will be a PGA Tour card-holder for the first time in 2027, told this week's GOLF Subpar podcast that his first golf memory was the 2010 U.S. Senior Open at Sahalee Country Club in Sammamish, Washington. He attended with his father and they sat by the 10th tee.

Bernhard Langer hit his tee shot into one of the course's many evergreens there. Docherty said he told his father that pros hit bad shots too. Langer went on to win that week, which taught Docherty that one bad shot does not determine the outcome. Sahalee also hosted the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.
Golf.copy:
Alistair Docherty’s first golf memory provided a couple of valuable lessons. The 32-year-old pro, who will be a PGA Tour card-holder for the first time come 2027, joined this week’s GOLF Subpar podcast and explained how a trip to Sahalee Country Club played a key role in his life.

Sahalee is a private country club in Sammamish, Wash., just outside of Seattle, and in 2010 it hosted the U.S. Senior Open. (It was also home to the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.) But in 2010, Docherty attended the U.S. Senior Open with his father, and they found a spot to sit by the 10th tee.

Golf.title: 'Fairytale stuff': Pro's hard year ends with ticket to 2027 Masters
Golf.summary: Grant Forrest has had a year to forget. But that all changed on Sunday in Spain, where he punched an unlikely ticket to the 2027 Masters. The post ‘Fairytale stuff’: Pro’s hard year ends with ticket to 2027 Masters appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Grant Forrest won the Open de España presented by Madrid, finishing 14 under to earn places in the 2027 Masters and the Open Championship at St Andrews. He had opened with rounds of 66-66-67 to share the 54-hole lead with Joe Dean. After going out in 2-over 38 on Sunday, he birdied the 13th and 14th, then holed a winning birdie putt at the driveable par-four 18th after chipping to five feet.

Forrest lost the 2015 Amateur Championship final 4&2 to Romain Langasque, which cost him a Masters place. His earlier DP World Tour wins came at the 2021 Hero Open and the 2025 Nexo Championship. He arrived in Madrid with one top-10 and three top-20s in 2026, and had not finished better than 63rd since June. He described the win as fairytale stuff.
Golf.copy:
Eleven years ago, Grant Forrest had a ticket to the Masters in his grasp. Then a budding Scottish amateur star, Forrest reached the finals of the 2015 Amateur Championship. A win meant not only one of amateur golf’s biggest prizes but also a trip to Magnolia Lane. But a 4&2 loss to Romain Langasque meant Forrest’s Augusta National dream would have to wait.

The wait wasn’t expected to be long. Forrest made the 2015 Walker Cup team and was expected to be one of Europe’s bright young stars. But golf had other plans. Forrest turned pro and worked his way up from the Challenge Tour to the DP World Tour, finally reaching the top European circuit in 2019. His first DP World Tour win arrived at the 2021 Hero Open. His next came four years later at the 2025 Nexo Championship. Along the way, Forrest played in two Open Championships and one U.S. Open, but never played well enough to reach Augusta National.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan's WITB: Full Titleist bag —including 3-wood proto — delivers again
Golf.summary: Michael Brennan won the 2026 Baycurrent Classic on Sunday for his third PGA Tour win. Here's a breakdown of what's in his winning golf bag. The post Michael Brennan’s WITB: Full Titleist bag —including 3-wood proto — delivers again appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic at Yokohama Country Club in Japan on Sunday, his third PGA Tour victory and second in October. He used the same all-Titleist setup as in his August Wyndham Championship win, including the Scotty Cameron Golo 6 Tour Prototype putter he switched to earlier this season.

Brennan also uses the unreleased Titleist GTS 3W Prototype fairway wood, which has now won three times. Like other GTS fairways it has a silver face, but it has only one sole weight port. It appears to have a larger, shallow profile similar to the GT1 fairway wood he previously played. Titleist has not commented on the club, which first appeared in March. His wedge lofts are 46, 50, 54 and 60 degrees.
Golf.copy:
Michael Brennan clearly plays his best golf at the end of the year as he just picked up his third PGA Tour victory and his second in the month of October. After winning the Wyndham Championship in August, Brennan took home the Baycurrent Classic on Sunday in Japan.

At Yokohama Country Club, Brennan used the same all-Titleist setup he used for his Wyndham win in August, including the Scotty Cameron Golo 6 Tour Prototype he switched to earlier this season.

Golf.title: 2026 Baycurrent Classic money: Here’s how much every player made
Golf.summary: Michael Brennan took home the title at the 2026 Baycurrent Classic. Here's how much every player made in Japan. The post 2026 Baycurrent Classic money: Here’s how much every player made appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic at Yokohama Country Club, holding off Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell for his third PGA Tour title in 12 months. He collected a $1.44 million winner's check and is targeting a place on the 2027 Ryder Cup team. Mitchell and Bridgeman tied for second.

Mitchell, still seeking his first win since the 2019 Honda Classic, missed a 10-foot birdie putt on 18 that would have tied Brennan at 16 under. Bridgeman, who won the Biltmore Championship last month, missed a 5-foot birdie putt on 17. Defending champion Xander Schauffele shot a final-round 4-under 67 to finish tied fourth with Brian Harman, Jordan Smith, Ryan Gerard and Stephan Jaeger. Amateur Koshin Nagasaki finished 69th and received no prize money.
Golf.copy:
Sunday at Yokohama Country Club began with a packed leaderboard and a world of possibilities. It ended with Michael Brennan holding off Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell to win the Baycurrent Classic, his third PGA Tour title in 12 months.

“Unbelievable. It was an unbelievable week. Japan was spectacular, the fans were amazing this week,” Brennan said after his win. Mitchell, who is still searching for his first win since the 2019 Honda Classic, took the lead on the front nine with three birdies and an eagle. But he dropped shots at Nos. 9 and 12, leaving him one shot behind Brennan coming down the stretch. Mitchell striped his tee shot on 18 and left himself a 10-foot birdie putt to tie Brennan at 16 under, but he couldn’t get it to fall.

Golf.copy:

However, giving game-improvement products can be a delicate endeavor. Nobody wants to be told they’re deficient in any area of the game, and the holidays probably aren’t the ideal time to poke at potentially sore feelings.

But for open-minded giftees, we love the idea of wrapping up a tried-and-true training aid. Here at GOLF, we’re always on the lookout for the latest and greatest tools to help you achieve your performance goals. Sharing is caring! So if you’re looking for some gift-giving inspiration on the training aid front, we’ve rounded up five best-selling products below, along with some commentary on what makes them great.
